Sustainable agriculture is favoured, with well - packed dishes: for example, the beef carpaccio, slipper lobster jus, marinated seaweed and oyster fritters.

Name: Au Fil du Zinc
Description: Mathieu Sagardoytho, the new owner-chef of the Zinc, signs a creative menu that pays tribute to painstakingly sourced ingredients (mackerel from Trinité-sur-Mer marinated in mirin, lamb from Clavisy farm, plums from Yonne). Remarkable list of Chablis (and other Burgundies).

Name: Au Flaméron
Description: In a cobbled lane opposite the church, Église St Maclou, a new gourmet haven awaits foodies in the historical heart of Rouen. Japanese chef Takahiro Oikawa, a devotee of French gastronomy, cooks up his brand of seasonal French cuisine, infused with Japanese accents. He crafts wonderfully vibrant no-nonsense dishes, such as pâté en croûte with confit octopus and yuzu, aubergine-miso dip, karaage-style veal sweetbreads, followed by silky custard tart for dessert: this chef has mastered every aspect of his art.

Name: Au Fulcosa
Address: 2 rue du Maréchal-Foch, à Fourqueux, Saint-Germain-en-Laye, 78112, France
Description: Fulcosa, which means "fern" in Latin, refers to the plant that once carpeted the surrounding forests and (rightly) suggests that the young proprietors have a keen sense of history as well as flavour! In their warm "culinary bistro", they treat us to tasty seasonal cuisine in which tradition meets innovation, e.g. Cajun-style poultry, green beans, white turnips, girolles and fresh fig. Don’t miss the house signature – warm soufflé with a seasonal ingredient.

Name: Au G'Retz des Saisons
Description: Well-travelled young chef Samuel Duchêne aligns his cooking with the seasons. His concise, neoteric menu, which changes every month, showcases first and foremost local Pays de Retz farmers and artisans. His score ticks all the boxes: hard work, audacity and flavour. Confident use of different peppers, without forgetting the delicious house-made bread. Limited capacity, so it's best to book in advance.

Name: Au Jardin d'Eden
Description: On the way into town, this eatery ticks all the boxes: an owner-chef with a fine CV – including 15 years at Le Grand Véfour, who has returned to his roots in Évian and generous, traditional cooking that keeps pace with the seasons. Fricassée of sweetbread and green peas; free-range chicken, lemon confit and roquette; tartare of Charolais beef; fillets of fresh perch…

Name: Au Koning Van Peene
Description: In the centre of an out-of-the-way village in the Flanders region, this place is an unexpected foodie haven: chef Kevin Barata and Lucile Prevost (partners in business and in life) welcome travellers into their inviting restaurant with an interior in which brick and wood predominate. The chef, who knows his stuff, whips up good simple dishes, such as lamb kofta, thyme-lemon hummus, barbecue sauce and kataifi, or farmhouse pork chop, cauliflower, horseradish, asparagus and a reduction of cooking juices. Lunch is excellent value.

Name: Au Marquis de Terme
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Surrounded by the Médoc vineyards, this contemporary restaurant is nestled in an outbuilding of the Château Marquis de Terme (an 1855 Grand Cru), whose terrace is set in the estate's pretty garden courtyard. Under the stewardship of Grégory Coutanceau, who signs the menu, you will taste fresh, modern cuisine that is very much of its time and free of unnecessary frills. The appealing wine list features almost 600 labels, including a selection of Bordeaux reds and prestigious vintages available by the glass.

Name: Au Pont M
Address: 3 rue de la République, Wissembourg, 67160, France
Description: In the heart of Little Venice, this former local butcher's draws crowds of diners keen to tuck into the chef’s culinary tapestry, guided by the seasons. Here, the ultimate experience is to dine on the terrace on the banks of the Lauter. The interior with a view of the Église St-Pierre-et-St-Paul is equally inviting.

Name: Au Raisin d'Or
Description: Located in a picture postcard wine-growing village, this inn, helmed by a young couple, strives to uphold Alsace traditions by way of no-nonsense, gutsy, wholehearted fare and premium local produce: presskopf, snails in garlic and parsley butter, Heimbach arctic char, beef in coarse salt, braised ham hock and choucroute... The ice cream is house made.

Name: Au Relais des Ménétriers
Description: This restaurant on the doorstep of Ribeauvillé is writing a new chapter as a new kitchen team reinterprets the culinary heritage of Alsace. The plating may be the epitome of modern, but the robust flavours remain nostalgic and traditional. It would be a crime to miss the desserts!

Name: Au Soleil
Description: Chef Anthony Schauer, who trained in top houses in northern Alsace, and his wife, cheerfully welcome you to their tasteful, contemporary restaurant, which provides the perfect foil to fresh, gutsy, seasonal fare with a bistronomic slant, such as seared seabream, white asparagus, kaesknepfle and a foamy hollandaise sauce, or a piece of French beef, veg, piping-hot crunchy fries and a béarnaise sauce. The weekday menu is excellent value for money. What’s not to like?

Name: Au Trou Gascon
Description: In the former HQ (from 1973 to 2023) of Alain Dutournier, who was renowned for his bourgeois cuisine with a focus on the terroir of the South-West, the revamped interior is more casual: open kitchen, vintage furnishings and a cocktail bar. The dishes are as delicious as ever, and some have a Southern French twang: think tortellini with artichokes, vol-au-vent with cuttlefish.

Name: Au Vieux Moulin
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Take a seat in the luminous dining room of this family-run house tucked away in the Graufthal valley and overlooking a peaceful expanse of water that invites contemplation as you sample the sparkling cuisine of Guillaume Kassel. Kassel may be a steadfast champion of Alsace’s home-grown produce and wild herbs, but he has no qualms about foraging further afield to discover the delicacies of other regions: Mallemort asparagus, Mas Schaller citrus fruit, Bresse fattened chicken, suckling lamb from the Pyrenees… The generous indulgent lineup unveils his talent and desire to please with one overriding goal: taste.

Name: Au Vieux Porche
Description: This building (1707) in the typical style of the region stands on the winegrowing estate of the manager's family. Her husband cooks up delicious classic and regional dishes: goose and duck foie gras with red onion confit; pan-fried veal kidneys with wholegrain mustard and house-made spaetzle; beef millefeuille à la Rossini. Cordial welcome.

Name: Au fil de l'eau
Description: On the shores of Lac de Miers, close to the Salmière spring, this restaurant boasts a bucolic setting with its terrace jutting out over the water. In the dining room with its floor-to-ceiling windows, warm tones and white timber rafters, guests are treated to seasonal, colourful and inventive cuisine. The chef subtly pays tribute to the terroir (Quercy lamb, Carennac green lentils) and introduces original combinations, such as mango piperade with the fish of the day or a strawberry-rhubarb floating island.

Name: Auberge Baechel-Brunn
Description: With Thomas in the kitchen and Esther in the dining room, the Limmacher’s restaurant is a family business! The chef favours premium ingredients, local whenever possible and concocts primarily traditional recipes with a welcome hint of creative modernity. For example, he proposes a new take of the familiar flammkuchen or adds a puff pastry Wellington-inspired spin to local venison, flanked by a gloriously velvety game sauce. The menu changes frequently, to the delight of the (numerous) regulars.

Name: Auberge L'Escale 87
Description: This Auberge by the former Route Nationale 6 is the quintessence of tradition from the warm welcome to the hearty food: Charolais steak and house-made fries, chicken in a pepper sauce with gratin dauphinois, Paris-Brest dessert. Pleasant terrace to the rear.

Name: Auberge La Grange aux Loups
Description: This village inn combines quaint old-fashioned appeal with stylish contemporary details: light stone, exposed rafters, wainscoting, a central fireplace and elegant light fixtures. The menu focuses on carefully crafted dishes made with first-class ingredients, many from local farmers: pollock in herbs, barigoule of spring vegetables and pesto of wild garlic, followed by a vanilla-laced shortcrust pastry, lemon cream and confit, dried strawberries and tarragon sorbet, which shows off the pastry chef training of the chef. Alfresco dining in the garden.

Name: Auberge Le Bouc Bleu
Description: Chef Romain Hertrich and sommelier Romain Lambert, after stints in top establishments in France and abroad, are at the helm of this pretty half-timbered inn. Pan-fried girolles with pak choy, pumpkin seeds and pine nuts, or seared beef chuck steak with onion and beetroot pickles... All produce are from organic or small producers. Thoughtful food-wine pairings.

Name: Auberge Le Cabaliros
Description: This pleasant village "inn" halfway between two famous passes – Col d'Aubisque and Col du Tourmalet – stands surrounded by the peaks of the Pyrenees. The menu features wonderful traditional dishes that are big on flavour and nicely presented: noir de Bigorre black pork loin, braised sweetbreads, Pyrenean trout. Pretty little guestrooms available!

Name: Auberge Lou Pinatou
Address: 242 rue de la Mairie, Solignac-sous-Roche, 43130, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: The picture windows of the dining room of this inn tucked away between Saint Etienne and Le Puy en Velay overlook a magnificent valley. Alexandre and Charlotte Roy, respectively from Le Puy and Marseille, seamlessly rustle up a spot-on score. Their gourmet repertory is invariably inspired by their orchards and hives and by their kitchen garden, that has grown year by year, together with a selection of mainly local ingredients: Arctic char cooked in wax from their hives, pleurote mushrooms from Saint Hostien and sorrel; beef from Haute Loire, carrot seasoning and stuffed morel mushrooms. A trolley of local cheeses and a fine wine cellar with a distinct fondness for local “Volcanic Loire and Ardèche” wines complete the picture.

Name: Auberge Metzger
Description: Successive generations have been at the helm here since 1885, each leaving its own distinctive signature on this historic establishment in the heart of the forest. A spacious, contemporary dining room provides the perfect foil to sample regional specialities: calf’s head and tongue, choucroute with all the trimmings, fillet of zander in riesling, while a slate menu offers a selection of seasonal dishes. Start your meal with one of their signature dishes, aniseed-flavoured snails à l’alsacienne, before continuing with a risotto of perfectly seared scallops. A cheerful, family-run vibe depicts the front-of-house team.

Name: Auberge Nicolas Flamel
Description: The oldest house in Paris (1407) is named after alchemist Nicolas Flamel. In a pared-back contemporary interior enhanced by its old stones and beams, the high-flying kitchen brigade of Alan Geaam is hard at work crafting premium ingredients into harmonious dishes in tune with the zeitgeist.

Name: Auberge Ramstein
Description: At this family-run place surrounded by vineyards, the tradition of hospitality continues from one generation to the next. The son, Lucas, who honed his craft in several prestigious restaurants, creates contemporary dishes with a nod to the Alsace terroir: duck foie gras, a selection of damson plums and toasted Gugelhupf; roast Alsace venison loin with cocoa nibs, pear poached in red wine and grand veneur sauce. The welcome is warm, the service attentive and they also have guestrooms.

Name: Auberge Sundgovienne
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Everything in this affable hotel restaurant is attractive, contemporary and cosy. The cuisine reveals a modern slant, orchestrated by a chef who is eager to please (sautéed fresh cèpes, loin of rockfish and fish soup with a rouille sauce, fillet of beef with morel sauce). Fine wine list and comfortable rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Auberge aux 4 Saisons
Description: Venture over the threshold of this large regional-style 1920s building with oriel and stained-glass windows into a handsome, inviting dining room. Poultry pâté en croûte and confit lemon; honey-lacquered loin of pork, cream of sweetcorn and sautéed seasonal mushrooms; chocolate soufflée tart: the young chef delights diners from start to finish. A concise wine list with a focus on organic and biodynamic wines; possibility of gin and tonic pairings (with local gins of course!).

Name: Auberge de Bel Air
Description: This granite-built farmhouse on the banks of the Aber Ildut cuts a picturesque figure with its large garden and lake. On the menu: the fish and seafood cuisine for which Brittany is so famed, eg fillet of pollack with lobster cream. A rustic setting in which to really unwind.

Name: Auberge de Briant
Description: The spacious and light new dining room gives onto the water and surrounding greenery. Tuck into the delicious dishes made by Filipe, the chef – pressé of Charolais oxtail and crayfish with sauce ravigote, sea bass roasted in olive oil, dill and garlic cromesquis... – and the tasty desserts made by Angélique, his wife!

Name: Auberge de Cassagne & Spa
Address: 450 allée de Cassagne, Le Pontet, 84130, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This gorgeous old Provençal bastide on the outskirts of Avignon upholds the hospitality traditions of the country inns of yesteryear devoted to good food and good cheer. Noble produce and classicism take front stage here, illustrated by loin of cod sautéed on a slice of bread with a trio of celery, leeks and peanuts, although the occasional more modern creation can also be found. Southern Côte du Rhône wines take pride of place in the cellar. Lovely terrace in fine weather and polished service.

Name: Auberge de Crussol
Description: Perched on the heights of Saint-Péray, a stone’s throw from the ruins of Crussol Castle, this former sheepfold is now a hotspot of regional country cooking. The meat, fish and veggies are baked in a wood-fired oven or roasted on a spit. The chef showcases local produce, such as farm-reared Ardèche veal and pork and organic eggs and veggies... The warm, rustic interior provides the perfect foil for big-boned, heartwarming victuals.

Name: Auberge de Grilly
Description: In a charming village between Gex and Divonne, Auberge de Grilly stands close to the church. While the interior decor tends toward the rustic, the cuisine is modern, with dishes based on fine ingredients cleverly curated into just one generous tasting menu. Service with a smile, plus a pleasant terrace.

Name: Auberge de Groisy
Description: Done out in a style that reflects today's tastes, this 19C farmstead is very charming with its exposed stone walls and beams imbuing it with plenty of character. It is the ideal place to sample indulgent traditional cuisine that focuses on local produce. On sunny days, take in the view of the Parmelan Plateau from the terrace.

Name: Auberge de Monceaux
Description: This quaint country restaurant, framed by wild flowers, sports a tasteful balance between rural charm (terracotta tiles and beams) and pared-back modern comforts. Two sisters oversee the front-of-house operations, as their partners pour their culinary enthusiasm into this cheerful family venture. Ripe tomatoes, crudo of langoustines, cocktail sauce and iced tea; free-range pork, courgettes with cockles, basil, horseradish and pollen; or Tropezian puffs spiked with Suze bitters, apricots and fig leaf-flavoured ice cream: polished, colourful dishes, in which freedom and tradition go hand in hand in a regularly changing menu.

Name: Auberge de Montpoupon
Description: A friendly inviting inn established at the foot of the castle of Montpoupon. The interior sports a fashionable patchwork of rustic (bare stone and beams) and contemporary details, while the menu takes you on a gourmet tour of the Val de Loire’s succulent produce. Prices that make sense and a terrace with a view of the castle.

Name: Auberge de Sainte-Maure
Description: Victor Martin and his chef Julien Drapier, a native of the region, are a well-established team. The intelligent and harmonious dishes beautifully showcase local ingredients, in bold-flavoured combinations, often with Asian influences, such as gyozas with a soy and ginger broth or the biscuit and matcha tea cream. Add to that smiling service, good value for money and a pleasant terrace by the water.

Name: Auberge de Valestalière
Description: This whitewashed roadside inn in the Cévennes boasts a terrace with views of the surrounding countryside. The interior decor is simple and straightforward (terracotta floors, wooden tables). Damien in the kitchen and Suzanne in the dining room pay homage to the Cévennes landscape and terroir and its produce (vegetables and wines): trout from Le Vigan served in a cold soup; chicken cooked with preserved lemon. Sincere and generous cooking.

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This restaurant at the foot of Ambronay's Benedictine abbey boasts a refined contemporary interior. The modern-minded chef-owner moves between the restaurant floor and the kitchen, showcasing local produce and selected wines. Opt for one of his set menus, which are served at lunch and dinner.

Name: Auberge de l'Abbaye
Description: A small medieval village. Tucked away from view, a 12C tower casts a shadow onto a stone wall, and behind this wall you come across this charming inn, which is certainly worth getting to know! Here they serve good traditional food that is at one with the monastic atmosphere of the place, all vaulted ceilings and stone walls.

Name: Auberge de l'Espérance
Address: 3 avenue des Sycomores, Le Buisson-de-Cadouin, 24480, France
Description: Desperate souls should rush to this restaurant that offers hope! The owner extends a warm and smiling welcome, and there is lots of attention to detail in the food, which combines freshness and taste. A reminder that it can be the simple pleasures that leave the deepest impression.

Name: Auberge de l'Île
Description: In this plush restaurant on an island in the River Vienne, chef Pierre Koniecko rustles up recipes that are both tasty and generous, such as his medley of lamb (grilled chop and saddle, confit shoulder pastilla). In summertime, the teak deck patio by the riverside is an undeniable draw!

Name: Auberge de l'Île Enchantée
Description: This former fishermen’s bar enjoys a verdant setting practically on the banks of the Orne. In keeping with the house traditions, the chef revamps hearty, wholesome recipes that keep pace with the seasons. Searingly good food!

Name: Auberge de la Chèvrerie
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Tucked away in the countryside, this tastefully appointed contemporary inn draws foodies likes bees to honey. The menu adds a tasty new twist to Alsace classics thanks to meticulously selected seasonal ingredients. For example, the goat’s cheese comes from the next-door cheese dairy run by the chef’s brother. The egg parfait ensconced in a crunchy nest and served with a frothy truffle-flavoured celery sauce is a culinary masterpiece and the nostalgic banana split is to die for!

Name: Auberge de la Diligence
Address: 4 rue de la Libération, Loiré, 49440, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A 30-year-old local culinary landmark, this delightful inn is graced by the cheerful personality of Tania Cudraz. Her hubbie, Michel, is a chef who knows his classics, as he executes a varied, individual repertory that is scattered with herbs from their kitchen garden and spices discovered on their numerous trips to distant lands, Asia in particular. Splendid wine bin. The enchanting terrace is set in the inner courtyard of this former post house.

Name: Auberge de la Fontaine du Berger
Description: This red-shuttered country inn built out of volcanic stone overlooks the countryside of the Puy de Dôme and Pariou. Tuck into a tasty, patriotic lineup crafted with top-drawer ingredients, such as line-caught Mediterranean bluefin tuna with a crispy wafer, or Lozère lamb grilled on a wood fire with a thyme-spiked jus. Don’t even try to resist the wickedly tempting house-made dessert: the iconic Paris-Brest pastry. A friendly greeting and a snug rustic interior set the scene in this affably French eatery.

Name: Auberge de la Forêt - Domaine de l'Éclaircie
Address: 276 rue des Verriers, à Lettenbach, Abreschviller, 57560, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This contemporary family-run inn nestled in the Abreschviller Valley boasts a chic and cosy new interior decor with a forest theme (since it is Auberge de la Forêt!). True to the seasons, the chef carefully crafts contemporary dishes: trout from the nearby fish farm, risotto with scallops and chanterelles, and the must-try hand-cut beef tartare. Make the most of the large covered terrace overlooking the verdant park.

Name: Auberge de la Marine
Description: In a small regional-style building near the docks, this young couple beautifully showcases local ingredients. Example dishes include pressed sea bass with sand carrots, chervil sorbet; fillet of hake, beurre blanc with sea aster, mashed sandy potatoes; baba with a citrus syrup, cream with lemon balm… Tasty and expertly executed cuisine!

Name: Auberge de la Poutre
Description: In the hub of a pretty village in the Jura lakes area, this family-run inn dating from 1740 plays on its rustic charm. Chef François Moureaux works with fine ingredients to create delicate and tasty contemporary cuisine, but doesn't neglect to revisit local specialities. As for the decor, the establishment is named after one notable feature: its 17m-long ceiling beam that comes from a 3m3 fir log!

Name: Auberge de la Rivière
Address: 2 rue du Port-de-la-Fouarne, Les Velluire-sur-Vendée, 85770, France
Description: A riverside location and ivy-clad façade set the charming rural scene for this Vendée inn overlooking the old stone bridge – ideal for a gourmet get-away! The chef works with top produce, aromatic herbs and subtle seasonings and each dish reveals the hallmark of his enthusiastic culinary quest. Make sure you save room for the desserts – to die for! A few attractive rooms overlooking the River Vendée are available.

Name: Auberge de la Roussille
Address: 30 impasse de la Roussille, St-Liguaire, Niort, 79000, France
Description: One can't help but fall under the spell of this fine lock - keeper's house, which stands in the bucolic setting on the banks of the Sèvre. An enchanting environment, but that doesn't eclipse the main focus, which is the chef's meticulous and well - calibrated cooking. Ingredients are top notch and enhanced without frills. A real pleasure.

Name: Auberge de la Tour
Address: 2 place de la Fontaine, Marcolès, 15220, France
Description: In the heart of a medieval village, this stone property with its corner tower and spiral staircase oozes charm. Renaud Darmanin has transformed a former café into a gourmet outpost. He only works with the finest fresh and local ingredients (sweet chestnuts, in particular), creating delicious, polished cuisine that skilfully combines local country produce with global spices.

Name: Auberge de la Vieille Église
Description: In this Breton "auberge" at the foot of the church, the charm of exposed beams and stonework meets contemporary cuisine. At the helm, Brieg Le Cam (formerly of Les Hauts de Loire in Onzain) composes dishes inspired by his terroir, which are both precise and instinctive. Proceedings kick off with lively and indulgent amuse-bouches – a crispy cone with coco de Paimpol beans, sausage and airy potato purée from the whipping siphon – followed by finely crafted dishes such as a medley of gurnard and carrots or buckwheat rice pudding. You'll want to return again and again.

Name: Auberge des Matfeux
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Close to the famous motor racing track, Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans, this family-run restaurant is decorated with abstract patterns and uses crockery made by a local artist. It was established in 1962 by the current chef's parents, and holds the Sarthe region close to its heart. Bringing to bear solid technical skills, chef Xavier Souffront composes flavoursome dishes that are in tune with the times, without shunning tradition, and highlight ingredients from his beloved terroir. Don't miss the langoustine ravioli, one of the restaurant's classics. The fine wine list is sure to be a hit with wine lovers.

Name: Auberge des Ruines
Address: 17 place de la Mairie, Jumièges, 76480, France
Description: In this pretty half-timbered house just opposite the ruins of the abbey, a friendly green-fingered chef showcases his passion for the riches of Normandy's terroir. Following the seasons, he fêtes ingredients such as scallops, sea bream and beef, ciders and Calvados, goat's and cow's cheeses. Everything comes from Normandy, not least the fruit and vegetables picked in the restaurant's kitchen garden – the chef does his own planting. With the greens and pastures of Normandy on his doorstep, he composes the magnificent cheese trolley using produce from neighbouring farms. Savour in an inviting and chic contemporary interior, or in the glass-paned extension giving onto the terrace.

Name: Auberge des Saints Pères
Description: In an elegant, pared-back setting, you can enjoy cuisine made with top-notch produce by chef Jean-Claude Cahagnet, whose experience can't be argued with and who leaves us in no doubt about his penchant for herbs and spices. Regular diners keep coming back for the high-quality matured purebred meats, presented in a tempting window display. The hostess provides a warm welcome and impeccable service.

Name: Auberge des Seiglières
Description: At the summit of a mountain pass between Uriage and Chamrousse, this stone inn with a commanding aspect has been given a new lease of life by a dynamic young team. Here, you can tuck into seasonal, regionally inspired cuisine without breaking the bank. Terrace overlooking the forest.

Name: Auberge des Églantiers
Description: A restaurateur couple – chef Kevin Bieber (who for a long time worked at Flocons de Sel) and his partner Mélanie Laugier – are the brains behind this fine little restaurant, whose terrace overlooks the Arly Gorges. In the rustic-style interior (think wood panelling and animal skins), diners tuck into delicious traditional fare, combining good quality ingredients (the Arctic char with sorrel comes to mind), well-crafted dishes and traditional mountain hospitality.

Name: Auberge du Bois Prin
Address: 69 chemin de l'Hermine, Chamonix Mont-Blanc, 74400, France
Description: In a smart, contemporary vibe overlooking the legendary Mont Blanc, Emmanuel Renaut and his team craft an Alpine score with a weakness for produce from the garden and the surrounding meadows. Mouth-watering modern dishes steeped in generous, delicate flavours: tartare of beetroot, celery and horseradish sauce; loin of roast venison, stuffed cabbage, game sauce; citrus fruit soufflé…The view from the terrace is particularly breathtaking.

Name: Auberge du Bon Laboureur
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a converted coaching inn built in 1786, this centennial family-run restaurant focuses on seasonal ingredients. Chef Antoine Jeudi certainly knows his stuff. Thanks to the small kitchen garden, there is always a veggie-strong set menu. A picturesque backdrop, delicious food and a fine wine list – what more could you want?

Name: Auberge du Cellier
Description: Deep in a Catalan village, local lad, Pierre-Louis Marin, in the dining room, and chef Yvon Rossignol, celebrate first and foremost regional produce courtesy of textbook technique and a distinct weakness for truffles. Their signature is a daring, yet accomplished vacherin-inspired extravaganza of melon, serrano ham and Rivesaltes liqueur. Authentic and bursting with flavour. Attractive lunchtime menu.

Name: Auberge du Château
Description: Christèle and Xavier Vanheule are passionate about food and wine, and put their all into making this Auberge a wonderful establishment. The produce they source from surrounding farms is bursting with freshness. While contemplating the peaks of the Monts du Lyonnais, you can enjoy dishes with robust flavours, including filet of Dombes duckling, split pea purée, grilled pork belly etc.

Name: Auberge du Château de Vaite
Description: In the same family since the 1960s, this inn favours wholesome nosh designed to showcase hearty regional victuals. Morels take pride of place, as do pike-perch and chicken in vin jaune, without forgetting frogs’ legs, fresh from the restaurant’s pond in season. Lovely terrace and service as smooth as a silky bearnaise sauce.

Name: Auberge du Moulinel
Address: 116 chaussée de l'Avant-Pays, Le Moulinel, St-Josse, 62170, France
Description: This peaceful inn between Le Touquet and Montreuil-sur-Mer exudes a smart rural vibe. The chef painstakingly selects the ingredients with which to carefully craft flavoursome traditional fare. House specialities include lobster salad, pigeon cooked two ways and Grand Marnier soufflé. Everything is prepared in house, including the bread and ice cream!

Name: Auberge du Paradis
Address: 70 route des Crus-du-Beaujolais (Le Plâtre-Durand), Saint-Amour-Bellevue, 71570, France
Description: Two restaurants in one! Chez Lucienne showcases a concise array of creative often spicy dishes to share: free-range chicken kebab marinated in ras-el-hanout; lamb gyoza in herbs and curry, leeks and soy mayonnaise; deep-fried scallops and tikka masala girolles pickles. On the other hand, Joséphine à Table features a wine bar with traditional starters and a dish of the day (marbled ham, pork pie, chicken kebabs, rice pudding). Both establishments boast a pleasant patio and a friendly, buzzy vibe – all of which washed down with tipples from Mâcon and Beaujolais and a range of wines by the glass from a magnum. Fans of Sunday brunch should make a beeline for chez Lucienne.

Name: Auberge du Parc Carola
Description: In this quaint, half-timbered edifice, a stone’s throw from the Carola spring, chef Michaela Peters continues to delight foodies. Along with her pastry-chef partner, she signs an authentic, inspired score: black truffle tortellini; venison steak sautéed in spices, roast parsnip and Grand Veneur sauce; baked apples with salted butter caramel. Pretty patio shaded by trees.

Name: Auberge du Poids Public
Address: 1 faubourg de la Fontasse, Saint-Félix-Lauragais, 31540, France
Description: Following in her parents' footsteps, Céline Taffarello continues to showcase the best of the terroir, with produce such as magret of black mountain duck with sarawak pepper and delicious, perfectly seasoned roasted peach with verbena. The cassoulet, which has won several awards, is particularly popular. The panoramic terrace, with its pretty view of the Lauragais plain is delightful. Comfortable guestrooms.

Name: Auberge du Pont
Description: Ten kilometres outside Vichy in a village dominated by a 12C fortress, this inn is near a bridge over the Allier dating from the 1930s. In a contemporary interior, the owner-chef signs a single set, market-sourced menu at a bargain price and a more elaborate score in the evenings: roast tomatoes in aspic, espuma of stracciatella in a gazpacho or a ‘blesotto’ of bouchot mussels and cockles with a shellfish foam. When the weather is fine, the shady terrace overlooking the river is truly blissful!

Name: Auberge du Pont de Rethondes
Description: In a delightful village on the banks of the Aisne in the heart of Compiègne Forest, this inn sports a traditional exterior and a modern, pared-back interior. Alfresco dining is bliss in fine weather on the terrace overlooking a landscaped garden. The score errs towards the traditional: pâté en croûte, veal kidneys in mustard, crème brûlée or soufflé to finish. The chef puts the finishing touches to carefully sourced seasonal ingredients, delivering an experience that is both authentic and polished.

Name: Auberge du Prieuré Normand
Address: 1 place de la République, Gasny, 27620, France
Description: Near Giverny, the main square of Gasny is home to this half-timbered family-run inn that is the epitome of rural Normandy. The chef favours local produce in his inspired lineup, flanked by big-boned sauces and steeped in forthright flavours. His signature dish, risotto of langoustines, is to die for! The interior boasts a bar, a cellar, two contemporary dining rooms and a patio come fine weather. Simpler, bargain-priced lunchtime weekday deal.

Name: Auberge du Prunelli
Description: A welcoming, cosy atmosphere reigns in this former coaching inn that first opened its doors to travellers in 1860. The Orlandazzi family has been at the helm since 1997 – today the owner's sons run the show. An authentic take on the flavours of Corsica: charcuterie and cheeses from the valley, vegetables grown in the village, stews slow-cooked on the stove, and wood-fired dishes – simply pair with one of their 300 Corsican wines. A timeless setting! In fine weather, head for the leafy terrace overlooking the Prunelli.

Name: Auberge du Rohan
Description: This traditional old Brittany farmhouse is located by the entrance to the Gulf of Morbihan Nature Park. The self-taught chef welcomes his loyal patrons with traditional, well-crafted, indulgent food: ravioles of girolles and foie gras, cream of mushrooms and emulsion of forest flavours or scallops sautéed in salted butter with a champagne sauce.

Name: Auberge du Sombral - Les Bonnes Choses
Description: In this house at the foot of the Château des Lapopie, you can be sure that good things – Les Bonnes Choses – are to come! Enjoy the pleasant cuisine du terroir, in which local ingredients are the star (lamb, foie gras, cheese... ). There are a handful of pretty guestrooms, if you wish to stay on in this village overlooking the Lot.

Name: Auberge du Vieux Gachet
Address: Route Gachet, au bord de l'Erdre, Carquefou, 44470, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The sprawling terrace, which commands a superlative view of the fairytale Gacherie château, seems to float above the River Erdre. A peaceful, refreshing venue set in the heart of unspoiled countryside. Even better, the floor-to-ceiling windows of the dining room offer the same fantastic view when the weather is less suited to alfresco dining. The owner-chef, Walter Lescot, works only with ingredients he himself loves: Scandinavian gravlax of salmon, lemon cream; loin of cod, celery and chorizo risotto and a piquillos sauce. The tart of citrus fruit and lime sorbet is delicate, flavoursome and fruity – an ideal conclusion to your meal. With over 350 references, the wine cellar adds the final cherry to this appetising portrait.

Name: Auberge d’Aillon et d’Ailleurs
Address: 795 route de la Correrie, Aillon-le-Jeune, 73340, France
Description: In the Bauges Mountains, an unspoilt natural haven, this contemporary hotel has a lovely restaurant run by a young chef who has both technique and ideas. He throws himself into his work to get the best out of the Val d'Aillon terroir: vegetable garden, cooperative cheese, farm lamb, wild herbs... The menu changes regularly.

Name: Auberge les filles en bottes
Description: At a remove from the village, this lovely country restaurant is housed in a secluded stone building. The bucolic and refined atmosphere calls to mind an old-fashioned inn in which time has stood still: exposed beams and stonework, antique silverware, copper moulds and dried flowers. At the helm, Lénaïck Geffroy in the kitchen and Louise Lefebvre front of house celebrate a simple and authentic way of life, inspired by nature and the seasons. Their single set menu, identical for lunch and dinner and regularly updated, offers a choice between meat and vegetarian. The aromatic cuisine uses plenty of produce from the kitchen garden: house-made ricotta and beetroot confit with herring butter, confit pork and full-bodied jus.

Name: Auberge à l'Agneau
Description: This family-run institution dating from 1902 is located in a handsome 17C half-timbered building. It is a great place to indulge in hearty food: in the kitchen, dishes simmer under the watchful eye of the chef, who loves his region. Stand-out dishes include local and meat specialties. Expect unpretentious, generous and authentic fare, served in an inviting setting… plus a warm welcome!

Name: Augia
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Le Vaugueux, an area of Caen beloved of tourists, a stone's throw from the castle, this restaurant takes the Latin name of the Pays d'Auge, birthplace of chef Grégoire James. The interior elegantly blends old-world charm – exposed beams, half-timbering and Caen stone – with refined contemporary furnishings. The modern cuisine takes the form of a concise menu, featuring local producers and organic ingredients (pea tartlet, goat's cheese, fresh herbs; Bayeux pork, sautéed potatoes, grilled courgettes, reduced jus). In fine weather, the patio terrace to the rear of the restaurant makes for a peaceful setting.

Name: Augustin
Description: This quintessential Parisian bistro features a small terrace on Rue Daguerre, well known to connoisseurs for its fine food purveyors and cafes. This plush updated establishment showcases a knockout, market-fresh score that is all about the ingredient. Rabbit terrine and red onion compote; sautéed farm-reared quasi of veal, seasonal vegetables with country bacon; rum baba to finish. Table d'hôte to the rear with a set menu.

Name: Augustine - La Table du Château
Description: In a handsome 19C abode near Montmorency Forest, this restaurant aims to uphold French art de vivre: period tableware and furniture, gleaming silverware and copper and high ceilings – all of which in a plush muted interior dominated by wood. The food is suitably classical and generous, whilst traversing the annals of French cookery: pâté en croûte, rabbit cooked in mustard and rice pudding. A few rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Auprès d'Angèle
Description: This lovely old house built of local stone is now home to a chic bistro complete with charming guestrooms – a delightful concept by Michel Bras and his niece Audrey Besson. In the kitchen, Catalan chef Guillem Bach and his partner Zoé pay homage to the recipes of "Grandma Angèle Bras", with an Iberian touch. Our favourites include the salmorejo with a hint of goat's cheese, Quintard poultry with anchovies, Granny's coquillettes with a dark chocolate ganache with olive oil cream, bread tuile and fleur de sel. The sophisticated decor features light fittings reminiscent of the grapes of Marcillac, a local vineyard whose wines grace the menu at reasonable prices. Dine in the air-conditioned room or on the shaded terrace beside a small stream.

Name: Autour d'un Cep
Description: This small house, whose origins date back to sometime between the 15C and 16C, stands between the cathedral and the River Maine. Chef Thony Pohu signs flavoursome, plant-led, seasonal cuisine with high-flying ambitions for the evening tasting menus. The cherry-picked produce is sourced locally and escorted by an extensive cellar of mostly organic and natural wines.

Name: Autour de la Table
Description: This venue calls to mind a culinary school courtesy of its purebred Gallic menu (ballotine of duck foie gras, beef fillet, Mirabelle plums flambéed in armagnac) and starched table service. Tradition and classicism reign all ‘around the table’.

Name: Autrement
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At a slight remove from the town centre, this quiet little restaurant lays out its own fresh vision. Working with quality ingredients, the chef has a perfect command of cuissons and seasoning. The result is original, colourful fare that is as carefully prepared as it is tasty: black pudding, onion tarte tatin and mesclun salad; beef cheek confit in red wine and carrot fondant. Don't miss his signature dessert, the Paris-Brest.

Name: Aux Armes de France
Description: This former coaching inn run by Yohann Giraud, a chef who has worked in several Michelin-starred restaurants, has a pleasantly hushed atmosphere. On the menu: dishes bursting with flavour, such as the signature macaroni stuffed with foie gras, celeriac and tartufata au gratin with parmesan, cream and a veal jus, or the oh-so-delicate millefeuille with a caramel sauce. The charming service completes the picture.

Name: Aux Ateliers
Address: 115 avenue de la Vallée-des-Baux, Maussane-les-Alpilles, 13520, France
Description: This warm buzzy bistro with a vintage vibe is always packed to the rafters. The chef, a Normandy lad who fell in love with the Alpilles, titillates our tastebuds with generous, down-to-earth cooking: Provençal-style stuffed veggies; terrine de campagne; rabbit leg confit in olive oil; shoulder of Maussane lamb baked all night long; two-lemon pie with orange blossom. A regular clientele and a pétanque ground outside.

Name: Aux Crieurs de Vin
Description: The decor is trendy with bare bricks, polished concrete floors and bistro furniture, as is the concept... Choose a bottle of wine from the cellar, before pairing it with a good, simple dish with a focus on ingredients (artisan produced charcuterie, free - range meat, cheeses from Bordier etc). A tasty and friendly place.

Name: Aux Lyonnais
Description: This bistro established in 1890 has a delightfully retro decor and serves delicious cuisine that explores Lyon's gastronomy in all its riches. The terrines, pike-perch quenelles with crayfish, and the chicken liver terrine vie with the specials chalked up on the slate, and the desserts are enough to awaken anyone's sweet tooth.

Name: Aux Poulbots Gourmets
Description: The rascally, iconic poulbots (street urchins) of Montmartre have now been joined by those of Thionville! Large bay windows, Lloyd Loom chairs and modern light fixtures add to the timeless elegance. The menu features recipes such as lobster salad and seasonal vegetables or pan-fried frogs’ legs…

Name: Aux Prés
Description: An unabashed vintage bistro in arty St Germain with red banquette seating, smoked-glass mirrors and floral wallpaper meets globetrotting cuisine from South America to Asia and Italy by Cyril Lignac, whose creativity nonetheless keeps one foot firmly rooted in Gallic traditions. Premium cuts of meat (rib of beef, shoulder of lamb) to share.

Name: Aux Trois Rois
Description: The bistro classics reign supreme (meat pie, calf's head) but there is still room for seafood dishes. The slate board features constantly changing dishes and the wines are real finds. A restaurant where taste, quality and conviviality are the order of the day!

Name: Azerole
Description: Originally from Northern China, Xin Meng runs this delightful French-Asian fusion place with a simple neo-bistro decor (stone walls, dark wood tables and chairs). Single-handed in the kitchen, the chef skilfully combines spices, tofu and kimchi with high-quality seasonal French ingredients, to compose dishes such as rack of pork, chimichurri, courgette cream and green curry, accompanied by a dash of creamy hummus and multi-coloured carrot ribbons tossed in an orange vinaigrette – delicious!

Name: Azimut
Description: This wine bar/cave à manger serves locavore cuisine whose flavours are drawn from locally sourced and, often, organic ingredients (including free-range poultry, snails from Eyrieu, lentils, fish from a fish farm near Châtillon-en-Diois, olives from Nyons). At lunchtime, there is a short and very reasonably priced set menu. To be washed down with organic or sulphur-free wines from a terrific selection – and the recommendations are on point!

Name: BOBY
Address: 150 rue du Forum, La Londe-les-Maures, 83250, France
Description: Set on a lively little square just 200m from the beaches, this charming spot gets its name from the owner. A seasoned professional, Boby single-handedly curates a menu with three options depending on what is fresh at the market – expect contemporary cuisine that is packed with flavour. Colourful, modern decor and attentive service.

Name: Baffo
Description: Originally from southern Tuscany, Fabien Zannier pays tribute to the flavours of his childhood in this small, colourful trattoria that packs a tasty punch. Fresh organic ingredients, often sourced directly from the producer: arborio rice, Colonnata bacon, artisanal pasta from Pitigliano and Italian wines.

Name: Baillotte
Description: Perhaps chef Satoshi Amitsu (ex Georges Blanc) is just being modest when he uses the term "semi-gourmet" cuisine on his website, because this bistro with an alluring red frontage more than holds its own on the restaurant scene. Deploying the precision for which the Japanese are renowned, the chef delights diners with pedigree Gallic cuisine replete with colours and contrasts, backed up by meticulous jus and sauces: smoked seabream, kohlrabi, fresh goat’s cheese, trout roe, fermented apricot dressing; caramelised upside-down apple pie, cinnamon-laced shortbread, cream cheese and rum-raisin ice cream. Insightful selection of wines by the glass that outstrips your average offer, with expert advice from the waiting staff.

Name: Bairoz
Description: Just a stone's throw from the River Loire, this charming, modern restaurant sports a striking decor with pendant lights, wood panelling and exposed stonework. At the helm are chef Estelle Méheust and pastry chef Jérôme Berdelou, both of whom are active in the kitchen as well as the dining room: one starts the service while the starters and main courses are being made, the other taking over when it comes to the desserts. This charming, discreet couple won us over with their market-fresh fare at lunchtime, and their more high-level cuisine at dinner: scallops, onion cream, marjoram fumet; pigeon fillet, squash and granola.

Name: Balafenn
Description: In a small village, this discreet old house that has been turned into a cosy restaurant also has a terrace giving onto a bucolic garden. The butterfly (balafenn in Breton) – the emblem of this restaurant and its cuisine – appears everywhere, from the decor to the flower beds. The chef's culinary signature is carefully crafted modern cuisine that showcases seasonal Breton produce. The monkfish with peas, carrots and cherry pickles is a perfect example: precisely cooked, well-balanced flavours and beautifully presented. The chef's wife extends a warm welcome.

Name: Bandiat
Description: The story begins as you enter this vast estate on the edge of the Périgord-Limousin Regional Nature Park, in the heart of Périgord Vert. The Bandiat, a stream after which the restaurant is named, meanders through the grounds. The large dining room leads into a conservatory overlooking the forest and bathed in soft light. The chef concocts a surprise menu which revolves around the produce from small local suppliers and his own foraging efforts. Assisted by a botanist, he endeavours to exalt herbs and mushrooms picked on the estate. A gourmet stroll through the countryside.

Name: Bar des Oiseaux
Description: In this small corner house, Armand Crespo's "Bird Bar" won't fail to have foodies flapping with delight. Fine traditional French dishes (brandade, bourride) feature alongside delicious artisanal pasta: ravioli and stuffed chicken, seafood linguine etc. All at reasonable prices, in a decor inspired by pop art.

Name: Bar mada
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: On the pedestrianised Place Saint-Charles, Bar mada has a terrace and a cosy interior with exposed concrete walls, a handful of tables, and orange-coloured banquette seating. In the kitchen, Matthieu Cambreling oversees a very "lively" biodynamic wine cellar; Italian chef Dario Ruffa presents small plates that exude spontaneity and freshness and are testament to numerous influences – every detail is on point. A vibrant spot where the food and wine are in perfect harmony.

Name: Basa
Description: This vibrant eatery is housed in a refurbished building that was once home to the commercial court. The original doors and benches have been integrated into the chic contemporary-brasserie decor. It is run by chef Fabian Feldmann (L'Impertinent in Biarritz) and Sarah Feldmann officiates as maître d'. The menu is evenly divided into traditional dishes (eg boudin noir and tête de veau) and more creative, travel-inspired options. Almost all the ingredients are of Basque provenance. The carefully compiled wine list embraces independent winemakers (with a particular penchant for organic and/or natural wines), all of which can be purchased to take away.

Name: Basalte
Description: Chef Adrien Descouls has set up shop 10min from his MICHELIN-starred restaurant and a stone's throw from the imposing 12C Romanesque Abbatiale St Austremoine. The bistro's simple decor – white walls and red banquettes – sets the stage for terroir-driven cuisine anchored in traditional recipes. As truffade world champion, he cooks up a generous, authentic version of the potato-and-cheese speciality with gooey fresh Tome, accompanied by cured ham. In the same indulgent vein, desserts range from artisanal verbena-liqueur-soaked savarin to peach Melba. The wine list features a wide selection of regional labels and spotlights a local winemaker each month. A lively and affordable spot in the town centre.

Name: Base Kamp by Aïnata
Address: Le K2 Altitude, 356 route de l'Altiport, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: Zaatar, freekeh, sumac, pomegranate, bulgur, hummus, tahini, mograbieh: French-Lebanese chef Alan Geaam made sure he packed his rucksack full of produce and spices from his homeland before heading up to Courchevel. Mezze and food for sharing, to be enjoyed – at lunchtime only – beneath the rafters in the spacious dining room, or on the terrace with views of the ski slopes.

Name: Bassas
Description: The Bassas couple, whom we first encountered at Deymier (also in Pamiers), has renovated this old town centre building from top to toe. The striking result is both understated and smart and provides the perfect foil to the food which shines the spotlight on local producers. Inspired selection of local wines.

Name: Bastion
Description: The team that has taken over this small Art Nouveau building opposite the Parc de la Pépinière is on a mission to serve as a bastion against "junk food" and the industrialisation of what we eat. The chef connects with producers to champion local agriculture, delivering vibrant cuisine that is, above all, packed with flavour. Very good value for money at lunchtime.

Name: Baud
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This family-run hotel-restaurant is depicted by a contemporary interior with striped carpets and crimson walls and ceiling. The cuisine, meanwhile, delves into the local alpine larder to craft a modern repertory: poached and then chilled Savoie trout, tarragon pesto and a herb emulsion; Muscovy duckling, celeriac, Roscoff onions and red fruit. Enticing wine list, a riverside terrace shaded by a pergola and snug guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: Beam !
Description: Beaming and buzzing! The kitchens of the Télégraphe, a high spot of Toulon’s cultural life, are all go! Energetic Arnaud Tabarec, born in Burgundy, honed his skills in prestigious establishments and was the star chef of the Five Hotel’s Roof in Cannes. Today he is acclaimed for his delicate, predominantly vegetarian cuisine, whose ingredients are of course sourced locally and combined boldly.

Name: Bec
Address: 55 avenue de la Vallée-des-Baux, Paradou, 13520, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in an old Provençal farmhouse standing in the shadow of a small church and fronted by a pretty courtyard, this restaurant serves fresh modern cuisine with international influences. To be savoured in the inviting rustic-style interior or alfresco on the lush terrace planted with oleanders and Virginia creeper. Your hostess and owner of Sardinian origins is in charge of the seamless service.

Name: Bec
Description: At this restaurant, Brice (the chef) and Élodie Collon (his wife) bring you modern cuisine in the form of a menu-carte revolving around Savoie ingredients: lake trout, escargot and pike, in particular, but not forgetting the optional foie gras, monkfish and veal sweetbreads for a small extra charge. The result is tiptop dishes packed with flavour, such as Mont Charvin pork pluma with polenta and barbecue sauce.

Name: Beefbar
Description: This is Saint Tropez’ delightful take on the beef bar concept that is gaining traction around the world. A stunning terrace overlooking the hotel pool allows red meat lovers and fans of exotic flavours to sample outstanding cuts of meat (wagyu and Black Angus beef), as well as dishes of South American and Asian origin.

Name: Bello Visto
Description: Gassin, which comes from the expression Guardia Sinus, meaning guardian of the gulf, is a former Sarrazin village occupied by the Moors until the 10C. After finding the house on Place des Barri, take a seat on the superb terrace and gape at the view over the Gulf of Saint-Tropez and the Maures mountains. Among the house specialities are rock octopus casserole; tartlet of red mullet; roast seabass with Sicilian-style fennel. This Mediterranean score is crafted by an enthusiastic veteran chef and local lad, whose grandmother used to live in the village! Food that throbs with flavour and a few rooms for overnight stays.

Name: Belvédère
Address: Hôtel Belesso, 34 avenue des Baux, Fontvieille, 13990, France
Description: Japanese chef Kohei Ohata skilfully harnesses the flavours of the Mediterranean fare that abounds in the surrounding markets to produce really appealing dishes. His talented wife brings her skills to bear on the pastry section. It is all fresh, fragrant and charged at a fair price. This excellent establishment is a little hidden away in the Hotel Belesso – reserved for those in the know, and all the better for it.

Name: Benjamin
Address: Four Seasons Resort Megève, 373 chemin des Follières, Megève, 74120, France
Description: At the foot of Mont d'Arbois, this elegant brasserie within the prestigious Rothschild family hotel tempts skiers, hikers and trail runners with its mouthwatering menu. Sole meunière, Rossini-style beef fillet, Norwegian omelette to share or millefeuille feature alongside linguine with cockles and house-made bottarga, risotto and even vegetarian dishes. Spacious and cosy dining room, attentive service and superb wine list.

Name: Benjamin Schmitt Restaurant
Description: This restaurant in Pigalle pays tribute to the land and those who work it. The youthful chef cultivates culinary eclecticism, seamlessly segueing from one style of cuisine to another and from traditional to modern fare. The enticing names of the dishes live up to their promise: duck, foie gras and pork pâté en croûte; farm-raised guinea fowl cooked two ways with herby aubergine and cherries in red wine vinegar; Tanzanian dark chocolate mousse with coffee-hazelnut praline and coffee ice cream. Wallet-friendly lunch set menu; tasting menu and à la carte in the evening.

Name: Benoit
Description: This genuine Parisian bistro still boasts its period Belle Époque interior (woodwork, copper pots, mirrors, velvet banquettes) and everything down to the plates bears the B monogram, further adding to the authentic vibe. Proudly and heartily traditional, the recipes star country produce: pâté en croûte, calf’s head with ravigote sauce, cassoulet, millefeuille pastry!

Name: Betton Fils
Description: In the centre of Saint-Malo, this little restaurant sits neatly on a corner, in a building sporting the characteristic grey stone of Saint-Malo. At the helm, chef Victor Betton, once a fencing champion, deftly cooks up generous cuisine. A devotee of fine food, he searches out the best ingredients within a 50km radius. At lunchtime, the reasonably priced set menu would win over any diner. In the evening, the à la carte menu showcases more premium ingredients (hand-dived scallops, line-caught John Dory).

Name: Beurre Noisette
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of Lucenay, a village built of Beaujolais golden limestone, this restaurant occupies a converted village school. Pauline Fleuret, along with her partner, front of house, keeps things simple in this inviting space. Her market-fresh cuisine is fresh and healthy, designed for maximum flavour: Comté croquettes, saucisse de Morteau and beetroot ketchup; chicken blanquette with tarragon and candied lemon, polenta gratin; lemon and sesame cake, mascarpone cream and meringue pieces. Reasonable prices. Booking is essential.

Name: Bienheureux
Address: 35 avenue de la Marne, Wasquehal, 59290, France
Description: In a red-brick manor house turned into a hub combining co-working spaces, offices and a garden, Lucas Grabowski (who after a stint at NESO in Paris went on to run Gabo) cooks up precise and creative seasonal cuisine: ballotine of sole with seaweed and roasted buckwheat; confit egg yolk with peas and herb broth. There is a simpler set menu at lunchtime, and an extensive à la carte menu in the evening.

Name: Biondi
Description: Near the Cirque d’Hiver, this gifted chef named his buzzy restaurant after a famous Argentinean clown, Pepe Biondi. South America also takes pride of place on the lineup which stars a fine selection of meats cooked over embers and desserts of the likes of a caramel flan with a dulce de leche mousse – to die for! Fine selection of Argentinean wines.

Name: Biscotte
Description: Pauline and Maximilien, two alumni of the most prestigious establishments (Le Bristol, Lasserre, Arpège), have set up their own place near Porte de Versailles. Convivial bistro interior, large atelier windows separating the kitchen, tasty and studied dishes: all the ingredients are in place for an enjoyable experience.

Name: Bistro Là-Haut
Description: Thanks to the hilltop location on Mont Valérien, this loft-style restaurant commands a superb view of Paris. The à la carte menu boasts a tempting range of contemporary dishes, such as hay-smoked poultry, vegetable tian au gratin with aged parmesan and a reduced jus. For dinnertime, booking is strongly recommended.

Name: Bistro S
Description: S like secret, savoury, sapid or Spinoza, not the philosopher but the owner who lovingly watches over this discreet Parisian establishment, and who is also a numismatist specialising in antique Greek coins and a genuine wine connoisseur. The talented Japanese chef Shimpei Oié crafts a fresh, healthy, balanced set menu backed up by his flawless culinary technique. Don’t miss the gilthead seabream: expertly fire-roasted and accompanied by white grapes and a kiwi juice. S like Super!

Name: Bistro Saint-Jean
Address: 132 boulevard de la Rochelle, Bar-le-Duc, 55000, France
Description: This ex-grocer’s shop is now a contemporary bistro, rich in flavour and colour, that hits the spot every time. The owner, son of a pastry chef, rustles up market-fresh cuisine in tune with the seasons, like this slow-cooked pork belly with baby onions and braising juices. Respect for the ingredients is the motto. Efficient, unobtrusive staff.

Name: Bistro Urbain
Description: At the helm of this spacious, light-filled bistro in the heart of Montpellier is Cédric Sangenito, a chef with a seamless CV and a firm grasp of classic techniques. His modern, somewhat inventive cuisine features Japanese barbecue cooking and lacto-fermentation. He highlights good fresh produce, especially seasonal vegetables from market gardeners, to which he devotes a surprise menu at lunchtime and in the evening. The menu is updated every week – although the rum baba, the emblematic dish of the house, is a mainstay (in various guises). A diligent and professional team is at your service.

Name: Bistro de Montcaud
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Château de Montcaud's chic bistro serves wholehearted cuisine with Mediterranean overtones as chef Mathieu Hervé shines the spotlight on local, often organic ingredients: Gubernat duck pâté en croûte and foie gras, mustard espuma; tataki of tuna and basil-laced humus; breast of Blaches guinea fowl, spelt risotto, green peas and St George’s mushrooms. A blissful shaded terrace overlooking the grounds, a warm welcome and cordial service add the final touches to this hospitable portrait.

Name: Bistro' 50
Address: 50 avenue de la Plage, Gujan-Mestras, 33470, France
Description: Just 100m from the beach and the port of La Hume, this modern, attractively done out bistro is the ideal place to share a handful of starters with friends or family, or to indulge in classic dishes given a lovely twist by chef Nicolas Vallois: poultry, duck and prune pâté en croûte; egg verjuice mayo, celeriac, baby gem and Granny Smith remoulade, salted egg yolks; pork confit cromesquis etc. The cellar features a good selection of organic and natural wines, as well as a fine selection of wines by the glass. When the weather permits, plump for a table on the large, pleasant, shaded wooden terrace and settle in for a relaxed meal.

Name: Bistrot 1936 - Domaine du Limonay
Description: In Saint Méloir des Ondes near the railway station, the roadside Bistro 1936 is the younger sibling of the prestigious Domaine du Limonay establishment. The dining room is decked in light wood and sports exposed rafters and picture windows. The modern mouthwatering repertory is firmly rooted in the region, courtesy of ingredients such as poularde (fattened chicken), foie gras and spider crab. Don’t miss the Breton curry flavoured mussels!

Name: Bistrot André
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The Pic family’s André bistro unveils a dialogue between tradition and modernity depicted by a spot-on score and bolstered by a truly outstanding wine cellar, courtesy of the gastronomic parent establishment, and high-flying sakes. The family’s heritage is celebrated with Jacques's mosaic of red mullet and foie gras and his orange-laced iced soufflé. Local trout gravlax is dotted with veggie and spicy touches, half-way between a vibrant tribute and fresh new start.

Name: Bistrot August
Description: A stone's throw from rue Gabriel Péri, two young chefs have transformed an old wine cellar into an intimate bistro. Trained with the Ducasse group, Léopold Gillen is to be found in the kitchen, while Maxime Renvaze provides cordial and attentive service, as well as recommendations from a wine cellar composed of some 100 carefully selected labels. This seasonal, technical and flavourful cuisine features perfectly balanced seasoning and carefully crafted details: pâté en croûte with foie gras, pork, duck and venison; hay-smoked duck, squash and juniper juice. Great-value lunch set menu and short evening menu.

Name: Bistrot Canto Cigalo
Address: Le Vallon de Valrugues, 9 chemin Canto-Cigalo, Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, 13210, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: On the terrace shaded by plane-leaved mulberry trees and overlooking the large swimming pool surrounded by a Mediterranean garden, it is a joy to hear the song of the cicadas (the "canto cigalo"). This restaurant – Le Vallon de Valrugues's second – puts fine ingredients centre stage in a relaxed atmosphere. By working closely with small-scale fishers, the chef is able to showcase fresh catch – a case in point is the superb wild sea bream. The lunch menu is more concise than the extensive dinner menu, which includes sea bass a la plancha with sauce vierge, Provençal-style aubergine papeton, Alpilles lamb shoulder confit with fresh herbs and a sweet spice condiment.

Name: Bistrot Coco
Description: Set in Strasbourg's old town, this contemporary restaurant with industrial-style decor is run by Constant Meyer, a young chef who earned his stripes at Le Crocodile and Le Relais de la Poste in La Wantzenau. He cooks up refined contemporary cuisine in a multi-course "carte-blanche" format (omnivore or vegetarian). Expect bold flavours and a friendly atmosphere.

Name: Bistrot Constant
Description: This spruce lock gatehouse, on the banks of a side canal of the Garonne River, is home to a bistro run by a meticulous chef. In a refurbished interior, Christophe Marque continues to champion wholesome bistro cuisine, courtesy of time-honoured classics faultlessly executed in keeping with culinary tradition – Bon appétit!

Name: Bistrot Cul Sec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: This tiny bistro on the Place du Palais is run by a chef-sommelier duo with experience in MICHELIN-starred establishments. The concise, regularly updated menu features clean, unpretentious combinations that hit the mark: grilled green asparagus, pistachio foam and praline; pork loin, peppercorn jus, potato foam, roasted turnips; a baba drenched in macerated rum, vanilla chantilly. With a blend of bistro and industrial style, the decor fosters a convivial atmosphere; the long, narrow dining room with an open kitchen leads out onto a terrace that gives onto the square. Some real gems for all budgets are stocked in the extensive wine cellar.

Name: Bistrot Francis
Description: When you name your bistro after your dog, it immediately wins people over! Here in the heart of the village, Antoine James and Sarah Mottay welcome diners into a space that exudes character, with terracotta-tiled floors, stone walls and a beamed ceiling. The chef rustles up enticing cuisine centred on local produce, with a Mediterranean lilt, but also other influences from around the world, for example Latin American: tiradito of yellowtail with lime and ginger, perfectly paired with a yellow pepper coulis. Laid-back service, welcoming little terrace.

Name: Bistrot Gros
Address: 18 rue de la Source, Nancy, 54000, France
Description: A youthful globetrotting chef runs this down-to-earth, laidback bistro in a cobbled street near St Epvre Basilica in the historic town. The bistro fare keeps step with the seasons and market availability, rolling out generous, appetising dishes, depicted by fried artichokes, frothy cantal cheese and confit egg yolk, or a fillet of trout with potato rosti, chermoula of cauliflower and an emulsion of Granny Smith apples. Natural wines dominate the wine list.

Name: Bistrot Instinct
Description: This pocket handkerchief contemporary bistro is in the hands of chef Maximilian Wollek and his enthusiastic youthful team. A market-fresh culinary score and updated classics with bistronomic overtones. Everything is homemade, even the cordials used in the unusual cocktails.

Name: Bistrot Loiseau du Morvan
Address: Hostellerie de la Tour d’Auxois, 5 avenue Bernard-Loiseau, Saulieu, 21210, France
Description: Opposite the Loiseau family’s legendary Côte d’Or restaurant, this handsome 17C edifice is both a supremely comfortable traditional hostelry and a bistro, offering an appetising more casual alternative to its fine dining parent establishment. Here, local and regional recipes take pride of place, such as eggs in a red wine sauce or chicken à la Gaston Gérard. The rotunda dining room, which leads onto a terrace, is the epitome of country chic with old terracotta tiled flooring and a glorious timber ceiling, all of which in an unabashed, full-on Burgundy style.

Name: Bistrot Marloe
Description: In this upscale neighbourhood on a street corner, Marloe sports a stylish, buzzy bistro vibe: parquet floors, wainscoting, mirrors, green bench seating and a red Berkel meat slicer in the centre, ready to prepare aperitif boards. Deft and fresh depicts the menu: carpaccio of seabream with summer fruits or cod with Mediterranean accents. The "black truffle" menu (in season) is a must. On-the-ball, cheerful service.

Name: Bistrot Paul Bert
Description: A bona fide Parisian institution for over 30 years, this bustling, vintage bistro serves honest, wholesome nosh to locals and tourists alike seated elbow-to-elbow at tightly packed tables. Examples include their legendary melt-in-the-mouth fillet steak whose pepper sauce more than lives up to its reputation. Slick, seamless service and a sensibly priced set lunchtime menu add the final flourishes to this local landmark that has been going strong for over three decades.

Name: Bistrot Racines
Description: Eugène Viollet-le-Duc found Chartres's Gothic cathedral to be the most beautiful in France. The owner of Le Grand Monarque Hotel had the inspired idea of opening this friendly bistro and wine bar with a terrace overlooking the imposing edifice. Locals, pilgrims and tourists dig into good traditional fare that showcases local farmers and market gardeners: pâté en croûte; veal belly, coffee reduction and fluffy dauphine potatoes; floating island served with a ladle, a French childhood classic. Savvy choice of wines from small-scale winegrowers.

Name: Bistrot Saint-Jean
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This bistro shares its grounds and chef, Olivier Valade, with Château Saint Jean’s other restaurant. The single set menu is the quintessence of creative bistro nosh: fillet of smoked mackerel, seaweed dressing and crunchy onion rings; tartare of veal, roast figs, red onion pickles, a crisp wafer-thin biscuit and shavings of smoked meat. The kitchen overlooks a long dining room and terrace.

Name: Bistrot de la Place
Description: In the heart of the village where Chabrol filmed Le Boucher (1970). Old stonework, beams and tasty country cuisine including andouillette and confit de canard.

Name: Bistrot des Falaises
Address: Place de la Mairie, Saint-Romain, 21190, France
Description: In a picturesque wine-growing Côte de Beaune village, this countrified bistro is piloted by a talented chef. The enticing score, which delves freely and regularly into the bounteous local produce, is as inspired and modern in style as it is exciting: flame-seared confit trout, Brussel sprouts, unpasteurised cream and dill-laced oil; barbecued squid, glazed turnips, umeboshi ‘plums’ and beef-dashi stock… Bouncy, cheerful front-of-house team and a weakness for natural wines.

Name: Bistrot des Hauts de Loire
Description: In one of the estate’s picturesque Sologne outbuildings, this venue sports exposed timber beams and oak floorboards. On the terrace, facing the kitchen garden, you will tuck into simple bistro dishes like red mullet, and more creative recipes such as sautéed snails with a bourguignon espuma and mushroom stew or buckwheat honey-flavoured chocolate tart. Ticks all the boxes!

Name: Bistrot des Rosiers
Description: In the lively Krutenau neighbourhood, a hub of student life and street food eateries, this down-to-earth bistro run by a close-knit female duo makes you feel right at home. Their market-fresh cuisine, in which plant-forward dishes take centre stage, is affordable and on point – perfect, of course, to pair with fine natural wines!

Name: Bistrot du Bord de l'Eau
Address: Hostellerie de Levernois, 15 rue du Golf, Levernois, 21200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A delightful rustic dining room with exposed stonework, beams and a fireplace serves as the setting for the traditional cuisine and dishes fêting the terroir made with vegetables from the adjoining kitchen garden. Dishes such as snails in a mild garlic broth, grilled trout and lamb navarin can be enjoyed by the fireside or on the riverside terrace. Open every day of the week, this convivial and generous restaurant is a real favourite!

Name: Bistrot École
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Courgette stuffed with einkorn and fresh goat's cheese; confit of Sainte-Victoire pork belly, mashed potato: a masterclass in culinary natural history, courtesy of a wealth of local ingredients, served up in an old schoolhouse. Located in the heart of this hilltop winegrowing village, with a terrace protected by mulberry trees, this small bistro is the brainchild of Grégory Brousse, formerly chef at Le Mas de Peint, and Alima Louange, his partner. As well as offering a full set menu that won't break the bank, the restaurant is also on point with its selection of local ingredients and wines (to accompany your meal here or to take away).

Name: Bizi Ona
Description: Chef Romain Lorenzon, whose good cheer is palpable right off the bat, chose to set up shop in this peaceful village. The premises have retained their authentic character thanks to their worn counter, exposed stonework and bistro-style conviviality. Armed with a long career in multi-MICHELIN-starred kitchens, not least Hôtel de Tourrel, he is now putting this experience to good use in a more free-spirited cuisine, uninhibited by convention and true to his beliefs: authenticity, simple pleasures and sharing. Hare à la royale, mallard duck pie with the glazed legs in a tarragon jus, palombe au capucin (wood pigeon flambéed with an Armagnac jus using a traditional cast-iron cone), Grand Marnier soufflé – his are comforting dishes to share with friends, especially seasonal game, a passion of the chef's.

Name: Black Bass
Address: Black Bass Hotel, 921 route d'Albertville, à Sevrier, Annecy, 74320, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A smart trendy vibe, a hip interior design and a sweeping view of the lake set the scene for bistronomic dining. Fish from local farms play the lead role in a concise culinary score strewn with creative flair.

Name: Bloempot
Description: Tucked away in a red-brick courtyard of old Lille, Bloempot proudly flies the flag of locally sourced produce. In a former carpenter’s workshop, parquet floors, glass ceilings and dried flower arrangements set the quirky scene. Chefs Florent Ladeyn and Florence Grave sign a highly distinctive culinary score focused on regional ingredients and unusual combinations: trout and grilled apricots, pollock paired with velvety courgettes and a buckwheat and sunflower ganache with malt ice cream. Big-boned, yet polished food, spot-on yet casual service and excellent value-for-pleasure at lunchtime. No telephone, so reservations are made through the website or in person.

Name: Bloom
Description: Bloom is an apt name for a restaurant whose Mexican chef, Christian Ventura, crafts vegetarian sushi! Breaded crispy rice, delicately dressed in vinegar with finely diced shiitake, oyster mushroom and avocado, futomaki and pesto sauce or vegetable gyoza in a kimchi sauce. The chef, a staunch defender of our natural resources, has risen to the challenge thanks to a lineup of vibrant and succulent vegan dishes. The interior sports a wood vibe rich in textures.

Name: Bloom Garden
Address: Bloom House, 23 rue du Château-Landon, Paris, 75010, France
Description: This restaurant channels the spirit of the Mediterranean generously, from the hardwood floors covered with Berber rugs to the wicker hanging baskets and zellige-tiled walls. On sunny days, tables are set out on the pleasant patio by the pool. The chef cooks up sun-kissed dishes using carefully selected ingredients.

Name: Blossom Bistrot
Description: From its location on the banks of the Seine, this restaurant overlooks the limestone cliffs of Giverny and the passing barges. A welcoming atmosphere awaits you in a pleasant interior with polished concrete floors, whitewashed walls and vintage bistro furniture. Gabin Rodes, a young chef from Vernon who trained at Éric Guérin's La Mare aux Oiseaux, revisits bistro classics without compromising their character, a case in point being leeks in vinaigrette tweaked with coriander and black garlic. A strong commitment to using local produce means ingredients are sourced from within a 100km radius. The lunchtime menu is a simpler affair.

Name: Blue Flamingo
Description: All aboard! Built entirely of wood, glass, steel and aluminium, this floating restaurant, akin to a 21C barge, stands at the edge of the Presqu'île André-Malraux. The bright, waterside space commands a view of the kitchen to the rear. The roof terrace has an appealing open-air guinguette vibe. As for the food, the chef rustles up modern cuisine packed with international flavours and bursting with colour and freshness.

Name: Bo-tannique
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: These attractive premises (with a contemporary interior and exposed Bordeaux stonework) are located on a charming cobbled pedestrian square. The fresh cuisine is full of contrasts and draws on influences from far and wide: grilled sardines with burnt miso and Lebanese-style tomato tabbouleh. The fine wine list features mostly organic and natural wines. Friendly service... A recipe for success!

Name: Boat aux Saveurs - La Table d'Annabelle
Description: This contemporary villa set away from the bustle of the town centre is run by a mother and daughter team. Foodies adore the lovingly prepared dishes fully in tune with the times. The chef makes a point of honour of sourcing ingredients from local producers and most of the veggies come from their own vegetable garden.

Name: Boccafine
Address: Place de la Fontaine et des Platanes, Nonza, 20217, France
Description: A small, listed village on the Cap Corse road is home to this demure restaurant, hidden by a curtain of Virginia Creeper and tall plane trees.
