The chef unveils his know-how as he crafts painstakingly sourced, local and seasonal ingredients, illustrated by ultra-fresh croaker, pancetta and pork jus in a surf and turf recipe of wondrous harmony. Love at first bite.

Name: Bohème
Address: 47 avenue du Moulin de la Croix, Mougins, 06250, France
Description: In this smart, trendy establishment with a decor of premium and untreated materials, the food is an ode to the very best breeds of beef cattle, aged and prepared by the famous butcher Alexandre Polmard in his unique way. Peruvian chef Manuel Rondan is in a class of his own when it comes to cooking over hot coals and wild-fish ceviche, as well as some lovely Mediterranean dishes. There is a drop-dead view from the terrace.

Name: Bolea
Description: In this 17C bistro, Léa Lestage (also at the helm of a.lea in the 18th arrondissement) crafts an intelligent bistro menu, weaving delicious modern notes into her unpretentious traditional food. The chef takes great care with the presentation of her plates and uses carefully sourced ingredients to deliver precise and flavourful dishes: langoustine bisque spiced with citrus and a fiery aioli; trout prepared two ways, with a sorrel cream sauce; chocolate mousse dusted with fleur de sel and drizzled with fruity olive oil.

Name: Bombance
Description: Pressé de bœuf (beef terrine), kale mayonnaise; roast mallard, glazed mini beetroots, confit legs; peanut chocolate, chocolate quenelle, ice cream and peanut praline: chef Guillaume Campion, like the pro he his, having worked in some of the best restaurants in the world, is embracing his role. With a sure hand, he delights diners with his lively bistro-inspired cuisine. In addition to the tables along the banquette, there are also larger tables, ideal for feasting with friends.

Name: Bon Kushikatsu
Description: This restaurant will whisk you off to Osaka to discover the city's culinary speciality of kushikatsu (meat, vegetables or seafood skewers, coated in breadcrumbs and deep fried). A low-key setting provides the perfect foil to the chef’s virtuoso performance: shiitake stuffed with ginger-laced chicken, foie gras flambéed in Japanese whisky and wasabi or brochette of wagyu beef. Bold flavours depict the evening omakase menu, while the score is simpler at lunchtime. The quintessence of Japan depicted by dishes ranging from beef sancho to spicy caramelised stew, a gracious welcome and courteous service.

Name: Bonhomme
Description: The trio who founded this lively bistro in the Faubourg Poissonnière are certainly not short on bonhomie! In this trendy, distressed-decor setting (stripped walls, marble-topped tables, glass-fronted cellar), the chef creates tasty modern dishes like trout raviolo, butternut, coriander, peanut and beurre blanc; Gâtinais chicken, parsley, glazed baby carrots, black garlic and jus, or chocolate mousse with salted butter caramel... Great atmosphere guaranteed.

Name: Bonnotte
Description: A 10min walk from the Albert Kahn Museum, Manon Negretti-Guichard and Antoine Guichard's restaurant has a simple, warm aesthetic. The pair of chefs have a solid track record to their names and pay homage to the Île de Noirmoutier and its famous bonnotte potato, a painting of which hangs on the wall. Manon runs the kitchen; Antoine also takes care of diners during service. The bistronomy cuisine gives pride of place to fresh produce and vegetable flavours: grilled courgette with feta and black olives; roast chicken leg (poulet jaune des Landes) with potato purée and a fragrant jus; apple crumble.

Name: Bord'eau
Address: 17 rue de la Poissonnerie, Colmar, 68000, France
Description: In the heart of Little Venice, this handsome regional edifice on the banks of the Lauch belongs to chef Jean-Yves Schillinger. A tasteful contemporary decor sets the stage for a culinary cast drawn from near and far: cassolette of prawns and Thai veggies; red mullet, baby artichokes and a rouille sauce with Alsace saffron; wafer-thin apple pie, butterscotch and vanilla ice cream…

Name: Boucan
Description: Chef Kevin Barata and Lucile Prévost (partners in business and in life), already owners of Au Koning Van Peene, are now also at the helm of the restaurant of La Barcarolle theatre. Neon lights and zesty colours make for a delightfully pop decor. The cuisine is straightforward and generous (especially the sauces!) and draws on emblematic produce from this northernmost part of France.

Name: Bouillon Baron
Description: Jérémie Baron's Bouillon is housed in a building dating from 1895. He regales a packed house of enthusiastic diners with traditional and popular recipes, such as terrine de campagne with pickles; devilled eggs, beetroot and vinaigrette; saucisse de Toulouse; calf's head with ravigote sauce; and chocolate cream puffs with pecans. The lunch menu, featured on the blackboard, is unbeatable value. A selection of wines, principally from the Loire Valley, includes organic and biodynamic options.

Name: Bourgeon
Description: In a converted cooperage in this fabled little wine-growing town, a young duo who were previously at La Rôtisserie du Chambertin have opened this contemporary restaurant with a personal touch. Chef Maxime Strassel and maître d' and sommelier Alexis Rappe treat diners to a minimalist dining room with an open kitchen and a few counter seats. The chef presents his contemporary cuisine, often plant-forward (foraging, preservation), in different tasting menus. Carefully selected ingredients star in precise and balanced dishes, underpinned by confident technical skills.

Name: Boutary
Description: This is just the spot to discover or brush up on your caviar know-how (osetra, sterlet and baeri), as the owners have been raising sturgeon in southern Bulgaria for several generations. A plush smart interior serves as a backdrop to the chef’s “carte blanche” menus and a very popular traditional caviar tasting session, served on the back of the hand. Former pastry chef of Ledoyen, the latter signs an outstanding delicate, low-sugar dessert lineup, illustrated by a coffee and caramel delight. The front-of-house team bends over backwards to satisfy and please.

Name: Brach
Description: In the luxurious setting of this former postal sorting office, redesigned and decorated by Philippe Starck, diners peruse a menu of Mediterranean-inspired dishes; these are executed with finesse and precision by chef Adam Benthala, who has an impressive CV to his name. The healthy and balanced fare embraces indulgence when it comes to sharing a round of kémia – small plates rife with aromas, spices and textures.

Name: Braise
Description: Wood furnishings, brick walls and soft lighting set the scene in this casual, lively bistro for meat-centric, flame-licked cooking. Against a backdrop of ageing display cases, diners sample simple recipes that revolve around the Japanese binchotan barbecue: perfectly grilled Baltic Black Beef rib eye, melt-in-the-mouth pâté en croûte or bona fide crème caramel.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Address: 15 chemin de la Croix-de-Montfleury, Corenc, 38700, France
Description: Set in a peaceful park, this third Brasserie Chavant has a large terrace shaded by a 300-year-old cedar tree, facing the tennis courts. The decor, echoing a tennis club vibe, features a green and terracotta checkered carpet, old Roland-Garros posters, vintage rackets and large bay windows. The kitchen brings a contemporary touch to brasserie classics and also serves the same signature dishes as the other restaurants – beef tartare, langoustine ravioli with foie gras and truffles, Angus rib steak with sauce béarnaise.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Description: Located in a handsome mansion near the Chartreuse cellars, this tastefully redecorated brasserie, which sports a striking white staircase leading up to the first floor, offers a patriotic line-up of Gallic fare, such as velvety Dubarry soup and curry; Mille Pas pâté en croûte; Dauphiné ravioles, among others. Tributes to the bountiful Voiron region abound, hence the melt-in-the-mouth slow-cooked pork belly à la Chartreuse and a decadent iced dessert, also perfumed with green Chartreuse. Delightful welcome and service.

Name: Brasserie Chavant
Description: This establishment bang in the heart of the city impresses with its chic baroque decor. On offer is a lineup of Gallic brasserie favourites (eggs mayonnaise, creamy mushroom soup, beef tartare, Argentinean Angus rib steak, magret of duck in a sauce à l’orange, fish with a beurre blanc and others), together with a selection of more high-flying ingredients such as the house signature: ravioles of langoustine, foie gras and truffles. Chavant was the name of the owner's ancestors, restaurateurs since 1852.

Name: Brasserie Constance - Abbaye de Villeneuve
Description: The brasserie of this hotel that has been tastefully refurbished from top to bottom, is set up in a space that is flooded with light through a beautiful glass roof and bay windows overlooking the swimming pool and grounds. The chef presents a menu that combines traditional dishes (e.g. pâté en croûte, egg mayonnaise, fish with beurre blanc sauce, Loire fish quenelle with crayfish bisque) with more modern recipes. We also like the attractive wine list with (very) reasonable prices, especially for the wines from the region.

Name: Brasserie Lutetia
Description: Tartare of wild sea bass, sole meunière, Burgundy snails with parsley butter: the famous Brasserie Lutetia proudly serves the classics that have made its reputation, as well as some more contemporary creations. Purists and regulars alike can't get enough of the easy-going refined Art Deco atmosphere. Conservatory, mezzanine or patio: take your pick!

Name: Brasserie Roseaux
Description: With this brasserie, Tabata and Ludovic Mey (whose other restaurant, Ombellule, is next door) prove that they have more than one string to their bow. Sit down to classic, bourgeois French cuisine: beef fillet with sauce périgourdine, chicken and veal sweetbread vol-au-vent, turbot with sauce bonne femme, savarin, millefeuille for two, cut and plated tableside… A tempting lunch set menu comes in at a lower price point to complement the high-calibre à la carte menu. The establishment serves the same wine list (around 600 wines) as the fine dining restaurant.

Name: Brasserie des Jardins - Domaine du Liziec
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Wheelchair access
Description: The second dining option at the Domaine du Liziec, this brasserie with bags of character wins diners over with its warm and authentic ambience and generous traditional cuisine. In addition to the weekday set menu, the thoughtfully curated à la carte menu showcases timeless classics such as house foie gras, lamb navarin, kidneys in mustard sauce, sole meunière. Meticulously prepared and bursting with flavour, the dishes are served in a light-filled dining room overlooking the gardens. And if you have to narrow it down to one dessert, the kouign-amann, baked to order until crispy, caramelised and meltingly soft, is pure indulgence.

Name: Brasserie du Louvre
Description: Take a seat in the sleek, spacious dining hall framed by floor-to-ceiling windows and revel in the quintessential view over Paris: Comédie-Française, Conseil d’Etat, Louvre… The enticing menu cleverly slaloms between hearty victuals of unabashed Lyonnais parentage (hot pistachio sausage in a soft bread roll, pike quenelle and nantua sauce) and timeless brasserie staples (snails in garlic and parsley butter, sole meunière, etc.). The terrace beneath the arcades of this emblematic Haussmannian edifice is sheer bliss in fine weather.

Name: Brasserie à 4 Temps
Description: A modern brasserie extended by a shady terrace, where you can enjoy classics that have been given a new spin by Franck Putelat's former sous-chef. House pâté en croûte, beef tartare, vol-au-vent or cassoulet… Rustic, wholesome fare throbbing with flavour. Book ahead to be sure of a table.

Name: Brion
Description: With an enviable CV (including Pierre Gagnaire and Jérôme Banctel) under his belt, chef Geoffrey Lengagne has opened this pared-back eatery (polished concrete floor, pale wooden furniture, open kitchen). A champion of seasonal cooking, he uses the freshest ingredients to deliver veggie-, fish- and seafood-centric fare. His modern signature is embodied by marinated cèpe tartlet with figs and cocoa, poultry breast in port wine or agnolotti of squid and braised cod, kohlrabi, pleurotes and a purée of Camus artichokes. The lunch set menu is a bargain - more elaborate lineup in the evening.

Name: Brioude
Description: This endearing family inn has been serving well-crafted food, in which local producers take pride of place, since 1887! The elegant dining room which overlooks the countryside of southern Ardèche provides the perfect foil to sample Claude Brioude’s “Discovery” menu: a new spin on the omelette with Ardèche watercress, gravlax of trout and leeks, trilogy of lamb with a veggie pie…

Name: Bro's
Address: 36 rue de la Foulerie, Blois, 41000, France
Description: This eatery in the historic town just a stone’s throw from the banks of the Loire, which has quickly been taken by storm by the locals, is the brainchild of two enthusiastic cooks and inseparable pals. The scene upstairs sports a stylish rustic interior with contemporary touches, providing the perfect foil to a bistronomic score that shines the spotlight on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients, naturally washed down with Loire wines. Tapas inspired by the produce of south-west France and Spain are also available (evenings only and without reservations) in the ground-floor room.

Name: Brut maison de cuisine
Description: This tasty bistro with a trendy raw edge sports an open kitchen, shelves filled with jars of fermented vegetables and books and only a handful of tables… so it's best to book. The chef, who comes equipped with a solid track record, whips up a concise, regularly changing menu. The three pillars of his cooking are seasonality, local ingredients and modern, often daring cuisine. An example: pork shoulder paired with white Paimpol beans in a tomato sauce with Kalamata olives and harissa. Interesting wine list featuring many natural and organic vintages.

Name: Brut, Table de saison
Description: On a narrow pedestrian street that gently slopes down to the beach, this discreet place holds its cards close to its chest. Front of house, Justine is from Le Touquet; in the kitchen is Alexis, who learned the ropes in Lille (Le Cerisier, La Laiterie). Together, they craft vibrant cuisine that is rooted in the Basque terroir and dotted with surf and turf references: a crispy cylinder of black pudding and langoustine, beef tartare and fried baby squid, red mullet accompanied by superb cecina from León. The desserts are just as accomplished!

Name: Brutal
Description: On a peaceful street corner in Lyon's Presqu'île neighbourhood, this neo-bistro has stylish credentials: a counter with a few seats, raw concrete pillars, an open kitchen behind an industrial-style glass partition, dim lighting, and electronic music playing softly. Chef Alban Joriot (Têtedoie, Le Neuvième Art, L'Établi) turns out seasonal dishes featuring clever flavour combinations, executed with precision and bags of character. Think white radish marinated in chilli, house-made pita, tempura vegetables; stone bass stuffed with wild garlic, braised sucrine lettuce, smoked tarama. There is a simpler set menu at lunchtime; more ambitious cuisine in the evening. A top-quality restaurant with a laid-back, trendy vibe: brutal by name, refined by nature!

Name: Bucado
Description: Brazilian chef Danielle Barbosa (winner of MasterChef Brazil 2020) is now alone at the helm of Bucado, in the location that used to be home to Būbo. To be enjoyed in an interior decorated with a colourful fresco inspired by South American flora, her dishes have a distinct character combining modern techniques (lacto-fermentation, fish maturation) and Brazilian influences (condiments and spices, cassava, tapioca etc). One of the set menus is vegetarian; classic cocktails. Attentive service with a smile immediately puts you at ease!

Name: Buerehiesel
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This picturesque, half-timbered 17C farmhouse was reconstructed stone by stone in the Orangerie Park, next-door to the Council of Europe. The conservatory dining room and patio command a bucolic view of this leafy haven. The menu features some of the house signature dishes, such as frog’s legs sautéed in chervil or free-range pullet roasted in a casserole dish (backeoffe), together with more contemporary seasonal recipes.

Name: Bulle
Description: Chef Guy Lassausaie masterminded the stylish top to toe refurbishment of this restaurant in a former Jesuit seminary (1853). You enter through a bar which boasts a jaw-dropping panoramic terrace, before heading downstairs into the restaurant, passing by the building’s Gallo-Roman foundations on the way! A swish, historic interior (crystal lighting, parquet floors and a view of the kitchen) sets the scene for colourful seasonal food, such as brook trout, fennel and seasonal mushrooms…

Name: Byblos Beach
Description: On the Plage de Pampelonne, this elegant beachside retreat was designed with sustainability in mind. Boasting a decor of bleached wood and cotton sun shades, it draws a chic, laid-back crowd. On the menu: delicious fish, meat from the wood-fired grill and highly popular pasta dishes – best enjoyed with your toes in the sand, gazing out at the sea and basking in the sun. At lunchtime, there is even a tender service, which brings diners ashore directly from their boats.

Name: Bürestubel
Description: This half-timbered farmhouse is brimming with Alsatian charm! Pretty regional decor and (very) local specialities: bibalaskas with smoked ham, bacon, garlic and parsley ; veal fleischnacka with mushrooms and cream ; sourdough tartes flammées…and the unmissable “real crème caramel like my grandmother used to make”.

Name: Bếp Việt
Description: On premises that once housed a brasserie, this restaurant specialises in Vietnamese cuisine that is entirely vegetarian, often vegan, down to the broths and sauces free of any animal products – a rare find in Paris. Summer rolls with tofu and lemongrass, rice pancakes with mushrooms, and banana blossom salad with tamarind… these are generous, aromatic dishes, in which animal proteins are skilfully replaced by a variety of different textured plant-based ingredients.

Name: C'Yusha
Description: Modern cuisine that makes full use of herbs and spices, created by a chef who works single - handedly in full view of the diners. Minimalist and intimately scaled (numbers are deliberately limited) in a resolutely contemporary setting.

Name: Caffè Cosi - La trattoria de Bruno Caironi
Description: Of Italian and Mediterranean inspiration, this bright, modern trattoria, housed in a former art gallery, overlooks a cobbled courtyard. We fell head over heels with the roasted artichokes in a pesto and parmesan jus. Before leaving, pop into the gourmet delicatessen store and stock up on top-of-the-range Italian goodies.

Name: Caffé César L'initial
Description: A large patio and a spacious, modern interior with an open-plan kitchen set the scene for spot-on, bistronomic cuisine, steeped in the aromas and flavours of Provence and the Mediterranean. Tartlet of rockfish and artichoke with sumac; dentex with parsnips and a lemon-cardamon sauce; chocolate opéra cake. A cheerful, friendly vibe with wines by the glass from a magnum bottle…

Name: Café Brunet
Address: 18 place Gabriel-Fauré - à Annecy-le-Vieux, Annecy, 74940, France
Description: This café dating back to 1875 is a real haven. It has managed to keep intact its soul of an authentic and convivial bistro (terrace, boules). As time meanders by, enjoy a good hearty meal or tasty little dishes.

Name: Café Compagnon
Description: After Richer and 52 Faubourg, Charles Compagnon, restaurant owner, sommelier and coffee roaster, strikes again! This cafe offers an extensive menu ranging from nibbles to share to home-made ices. The original, deftly crafted recipes feature a modern bistro slant, depicted by market-fresh starters and succulent loin of pork. Heart-warming, authentic comfort food.

Name: Café César
Description: In a quiet little street, opposite a park, Café César is a modern bistro with a colourful, light-filled interior (red bricks, some painted white, blue zellige tiled counter, polished concrete flooring). From morning to night, people come and go, for coffee, lunch or dinner, the common thread being the precise and carefully prepared cuisine. The sauces and gravies, prepared to exacting standards, give layers of flavour to the dishes – crabmeat enhanced with curry, scallops served with a creamy fish roe sauce, or hot chocolate tartlet. Everything served here is house-made, the service is relaxed and, at lunchtime, the bill is more than reasonable. As Henry Miller would say, "Quiet Days in Clichy"!

Name: Café Roma
Description: Italia Palladino's second restaurant (the other being Italie là-bas Ré), Café Roma boasts a prime location in the historical centre, at the foot of one of the towers of the Palais des Papes – admire the view from the terrace. The colourful interior decor with large golden mirrors adds to the charm. The dishes showcase the generous and fragrant flavours of the Mediterranean, incorporating the occasional Asian influence.

Name: Café Terroir
Description: Established near the Célestins Theatre, under the auspices of Jean-François Têtedoie (son of legendary Christian!), this house upholds the art of good food. The menu reads like a culinary bible of Lyon’s specialties: signature dishes like homemade terrine and gâteau lyonnais rub shoulders with rotisserie joints, to be shared and carved in front of you (Bresse poultry, rib of beef), without forgetting a lineup of bistro classics such as calf’s sweetbread vol-au-vent or Monts du Lyonnais snails with girolle mushrooms and cress. The wine cellar boasts over 1,500 references at temptingly reasonable prices.

Name: Café Terroir Chez Saint-Cyr
Description: The twin of the Lyon Café Terroir, this restaurant is located in the grounds of Domaine Saint-Cyr, the wine estate in Anse, on the edge of the Beaujolais area. A new take on Lyon specialities, excellent roast meats for sharing and an extensive wine list, on which the estate takes centre stage alongside vintages from Beaujolais and other terroirs, all from independent winegrowers. The place has a rustic and welcoming bistro feel and a terrace looking out onto the surrounding countryside.

Name: Café de la Fontaine
Address: 4 avenue du Général-de-Gaulle, La Turbie, 06320, France
Description: Taken over by a duo of young professionals, Café de la Fontaine has been given a new lease of life without losing the nostalgic charm of a village café. The menu revolves around nicely crafted bistro classics: house-made country terrine seasoned with five-peppercorn mix, stuffed cabbage, onglet steak with marchand de vin sauce, pearly cod loin and petits pois à la parisienne, seasonal clafoutis.

Name: Café des Ministères
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
Description: This neighbourhood cafe-inspired bistro is a firm favourite with fans of authentic French cuisine (especially from the south-west) and knockout sauces. Vol-au-vent with sweetbread, poultry and truffle jus, as well as stuffed Pontoise cabbage (French champion in 2022) are among its signature dishes. Now add a fine selection of wines from all over France, painstakingly curated by Roxane, the chef’s wine-buff wife, who can be relied upon for her inspired insights. Bookings highly recommended.

Name: Calcifer
Description: Forget fire demons and infernos – here it's all about the art of wood-fired cooking, with mouth-watering dishes prepared in plain sight in the open kitchen of this neo-vintage bistro. In the lively atmosphere of the dining room with delightfully retro mosaic tiling, or in the privacy of a booth, tuck into superb whole cuts (eg turbot, matured Galician sirloin steak or Burgos suckling pig) served simply on stainless steel platters for sharing, accompanied by smoked lettuce or grilled seasonal vegetables. A warm welcome.

Name: Calice
Description: The team from Baillote strikes again! Located in a narrow, picturesque little street, this convivial restaurant boasts a dining area done out in ochre tones and with leather banquette seating, an open kitchen with a counter and a back room with a skylight. Chef Louis Fedide (who has worked at Le Gavroche in London) is winning over diners with modern cuisine that combines French ingredients with the flavours of Japan – the influence of co-owner Kazuma Chikuda makes itself felt here. He cooks his pork tenderloin, cherry jus, pommes Anna and pak choi, for example, over binchotan charcoal. Delicious lunchtime menu-carte; in the evening, enticing small plates and fine cuts of meat and fish to share.

Name: Cambrousse - Château de la Bûcherie
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This 19C property stands on the edge of the Vexin region, and it is well worth taking a stroll in the 65ha of listed parkland that surrounds it with meadows, streams and lakes. In the cellar room with its vaulted stone ceiling, a chef who honed his skills in Alain Ducasse's establishments lets the ingredients do the talking. These are harvested from the estate's 3 000m2 permaculture garden, complete with a chicken coop and beehives; the Atlantic region provides the rest – Noirmoutier potatoes, red seabream and line-caught bluefin tuna. It is the season that calls the shots when it comes to the simple, unfussy dishes, many of which are cooked over a wood fire for added depth and character.

Name: Campagne, Vignes et Gourmandises
Address: 629 chemin des Terres, route de Suze-la-Rousse, Sainte-Cécile-les-Vignes, 84290, France
Description: With its atmosphere blending rustic charm (exposed stones, painted wooden furniture) and modern touches (contemporary paintings), this restaurant has bags of character. In the kitchen, chef Sylvain Fernandes prepares fresh ingredients in a subtle celebration of the flavours of the South of France. Extremely courteous service provided by Sylvia, the chef's wife!

Name: Campelli
Description: This diminutive restaurant with a midnight-blue and gold façade boasts a chic yet understated decor, all the better to showcase the creative cuisine and multicultural culinary experience of chef Vartivar Jarkezian. Firmly rooted in French tradition, his cooking also draws discreetly on the influences and pantry of the Middle East (cumin, pistachio, turmeric, yoghurt sauce).

Name: Camélia
Address: 1 allée des Camélias, La Baule, 44500, France
Description: Nestled a stone's throw from Avenue du Général-de-Gaulle, this colourful little place gives pride of place to local and seasonal produce on its blackboard menu. Laurent Chauvin – who founded La Tête de l'Art in Guérande – cooks with sincerity and generosity: divine house-made terrine, roasted monkfish served on a bed of caramelised shallot Tatin, and the strawberry tart provides a refreshing finish. Closely arranged tables foster a convivial atmosphere at this indulgent restaurant.

Name: Canaima
Description: This tiny restaurant sports a trendy interior. Only open in the evening, it is run by a delightful couple and serves fusion cuisine that straddles South America and France. The Venezuelan chef, who trained at the Paul Bocuse Institute, whips up flavoursome dishes rich in surprise and colour: croquetas of prawns, vegetarian patacon, dulce de leche and corn cake. Mainly Chilean and Argentinean wines. Cheerful service and a casual vibe.

Name: Canova
Description: Here in the Old Town, a chef from Milan who settled in France many years ago serves "gastronomie de rue" (elevated street food) – a fusion of Latin American, North African and Asian flavours. Francesco's colourful dishes are packed with spice: cod, smoked garlic cream, cockles and chorizo; beef consommé and carpaccio, noodles and fresh herbs. Good value for money means that customers keep coming back. Booking required.

Name: Cantine et Canons
Description: This old crêperie in Morgat, once a sardine and tuna fishing port and part of Crozon, has been given a new lease of life by a young couple. In their convivial restaurant with an open kitchen, the short seasonal menu on the slate board sets the tone: red mullet and a rich, full-flavoured soup, pollock with butternut French toast, or peanut cream, chocolate ganache and sesame caramel. More than 100 wines are available by the glass at thirst-quenching prices: a trove of unusual combinations to look forward to!

Name: Cap de Castel
Description: Take a seat on the splendid terrace with the Pyrenees in the distance and the Montagne Noire in the foreground and get ready to sample modern cuisine with traditional touches. The food highlights local produce, such as veal raised in Puylaurens, lightly seared and served rare with Veggie Wellington and a coffee-flavoured veal gravy. Lovely guestrooms to prolong your stay in style.

Name: Carpe Diem
Description: Run by a couple in their thirties (Jean-François in the kitchen, Clémentine on desserts and in charge of service), this small bistro has beautifully preserved its vintage soul. The subtly refreshed interior charms with its textured plastered walls, banquette seating, and painted panels from 1936. Expect an affordable menu-carte of traditionally inspired, gently modernised dishes: house-made pâté en croûte, salmon trout with a tarragon stuffing and lobster bisque, and chocolate millefeuille...

Name: Carré des Sens
Description: In a pretty spot on one of the city's central squares, this building is the stomping ground of a chef who revisits classics from French tradition with passion and precision: boiled egg, fricassee of chanterelles and parsley emulsion; chuck of beef cooked at a low temperature, potato galette and truffle jus; hot soufflé with Grand Marnier – quality ingredients go into these delicious and carefully executed dishes.

Name: Casa Fuego
Address: 80 bis boulevard de Garavan, Menton, 06500, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Just opposite Mauro Colagreco's flagship restaurant, this is the Italian-Argentine chef's hacienda-style Argentinian grill, which has a large covered terrace overlooking the sea, the town and the harbour. You are completely transported by this typically Argentine open-flame cooking, which here is well executed and so delicious, with its smoky aromas: empanadas, octopus a la plancha, beef picanha to share, dulce de leche flan. A masterclass in gourmet conviviality.

Name: Casa Verde
Description: Set in a small building of local stone, this restaurant is reminiscent of a forester's lodge with its exposed stone or forest-green walls, wooden ceilings and beams. Two brothers – one in the kitchen, the other front of house – bring warmth to this wood-rich building, the name of which pays tribute to their grandfather, who was a forest ranger in Spain. Their subtly creative cuisine sees a fusion of local and Iberian influences and nods to Japan – a country that inspires this inseparable pair. The picanha kakushi-bocho (knife-cut beef), kasha and lacto-fermented chimichurri are fine examples of their indulgent style. Remember to reserve your table – it's often fully booked!

Name: Cascade
Address: 26 cour de la Filature, Salles-la-Source, 12330, France
Description: What a pretty village clinging to a cliff and famous for its cooling waterfall! What a pleasant, convivial place, with its warm, colourful bistro decor, lovely old wooden floorboards, counter and arty posters on the walls (and let's not forget the terrace overlooking the courtyard in front of the town hall). In the kitchen, chef Marine Guichou cooks up a feast, using carefully selected local produce, which she skilfully prepares in a fresh, authentic bistro style.

Name: Case.
Description: In the old town of Tours, a young couple have breathed new life into this 15C building. The interior decor is now a blend of contemporary style and original architecture: whitewashed and brown stucco-clad walls, zellige tiles, white metal chairs with mesh backs and stainless steel tables. Mélanie Cases, formerly a textile product manager with a passion for art, designed the ceramic tableware and linen herself. In the kitchen, Rodolphe Boidron, with a wealth of experience in high-calibre establishments (Le Lucé, Auberge du Bon Laboureur, Les Hautes Roches), skilfully crafts creative, delicious bistro cuisine, using local ingredients as and when they are available, for example veal knuckle, peas, broad beans, sage juice and fregola. Very pleasant terrace on a small square.

Name: Casse-Cailloux
Description: This gourmet bistro is established in a residential neighbourhood near Prébendes garden and flanked by a summer terrace. The posters and vinyls on the walls and the buzzy, down-to-earth vibe are the work of the owners, both rock music fans. The slate menu depicts a lineup of seasonal recipes, cooked indulgently and authentically and ideally paired with one of the establishment’s well-chosen Loire tipples. Marinated aubergines, cecina of beef and scamoza; fillets of red mullet, morcilla of Asturia (black pudding) and chickpea bouillabaisse. Bookings highly advisable.

Name: Cassis
Description: After stints in prestigious establishments, this chef excels at meticulous, tasty, straight-forward cuisine, starring quality ingredients (meat from Haute-Loire, vegetables from a local market gardener). The regularly renewed lunchtime menu is a steal; in the evening a mystery menu is paired with a splendid lineup of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages.

Name: Castel Ac'h
Description: Brittany is full of magical places and the Abers region is one such! Just a stone’s throw from the lighthouses of Ile Vierge and Ile de Wrac’h, this handsome neo-Brittany house enjoys a superb location opposite the picturesque Lilia Beach. The food is of regional inspiration with a range of tasty surf and turf ingredients and the lunchtime menu is a steal. In the evening, two set menus and one à la carte play a bistronomic Brittany score: oysters, abalone, fish of the day, veggies from the cottage garden, seaweed and sarrazin wheat...

Name: Castel Damandre
Address: 18 rue de la Cascade, Les Planches-près-Arbois, 39600, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: At the end of a lane in the scenic village of Les Planches, you are greeted by a magnificent hamlet of old stone buildings, including a 15C mill, turned into a papermill in the 19C. The traditional dining room, complete with a flagged stone floor and a fireplace, oozes with charm, while the terrace overlooking Cuisance waterfall is truly jaw-dropping. The chef errs towards traditional recipes by way of a very concise menu. Trout in particular takes the limelight, illustrated by a tartare of trout with exotic fruits, yuzu, mango sorbet, passion fruit and coriander. The chef’s signature dish is a consummate ballotine of Bresse hen in morel mushrooms and vin jaune – to die for!

Name: Castel de Très Girard
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Housed in a former wine press in the heart of a wine-growing village, this contemporary bistro charms with its bright space overlooking the terrace and garden. The atmosphere is relaxed and the modern cuisine is rife with clever combinations, such as beef tartare and oysters enhanced with fresh herbs and citrus jelly; red tuna loin with lardo di Colonnata, artichoke and Parmesan. The wine list is a major draw: extensive, lively and with regional labels at its heart, it gives you an opportunity to discover small appellations from renowned winemakers as well as to taste great vintages by the glass. Open every day for lunch and dinner!

Name: Cave et Cuisine
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A townhouse with blue shutters next to the church, a remarkable wine cellar and a chef who is following in the family tradition. An undeniable talent in the kitchen, she combines classics (eggs in a red wine sauce, ham hock terrine with parsley etc), contemporary dishes (salmon gravlax) and specialities such as roast pigeon or veal sweetbreads. To be savoured in a refined bistro decor, where friendly service is the order of the day and the wine recommendations are on point.

Name: Caves Madeleine
Description: A stone's throw from the town centre, this wine bar-restaurant is a little gem. Chef Martial has hooked up with the best local producers, including some top wine growers, to create wholesome, punchy cuisine that is rife with flavour, eg warm potatoes, haddock, and tarragon sabayon. Relaxed, no-fuss service – the focus is firmly on the contents of your glass and your plate. In fine weather, make the most of the pleasant terrace in the shade of a fig tree.

Name: Caves Pétrissans
Description: This splendid family business has seen successive generations of the Allemoz dynasty at the helm since 1895. Treat yourself to a chicken liver pâté with onion jam, grilled hanger steak or calf’s head with a ravigote sauce. Bistro classics also depict the dessert lineup, with regressive dishes like rum baba or île flottante. An enticing wine list adds the final cherry to this appetising programme.

Name: Cayola
Address: 76 promenade de Cayola, anse de Cayola, Château-d'Olonne, 85180, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: From the dining room and the terrace, the view of the Atlantic is superb, enough to inspire dreams of embarking on a long cruise. But escapism is to be had in the dishes, where seafood ingredients reign supreme: salmon confit at 54°C, organic fennel from Les Jardins de la Chaume; Challans poultry, aubergine, Parmesan and chanterelles.

Name: Caïus
Description: This discreet, low-key restaurant, a stone’s throw from the Étoile, sports two dining atmospheres: metal and leather on one side, and velvet and light wood with a view of the kitchen, on the other. The bistronomic-inclined score is market fresh and good value for money: vol-au-vent, guinea fowl and Albufera sauce; braised beef cheeks in green pepper, mashed potato and charred onions with button mushrooms…

Name: Celest
Address: Radisson Blu Lyon, 129 rue Servient, Lyon, 69003, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: On the 32nd floor of the Part-Dieu Tower, aka as "The Pencil", admire the jaw-dropping cityscape while sampling a seasonal menu signed by talented chef Aude Andrillat. Her up-to-the-minute, inspired repertory unveils high-flying, delicate technique and a genuine flair for contrasts, illustrated in particular by her work with vegetables and seasonings and her knack for blending vibrant ingredients. An example: confit scallops in a vanilla-laced butter, lovage-flavoured soubise sauce and a praliné of squash seeds. Heroically irreverent!

Name: Cercle
Description: South of Perpignan, this contemporary restaurant is on the upper floor of an old building with exposed stone and brick walls. A multi-course single set menu is served at a horseshoe-shaped counter that opens onto the kitchen. Chef Julien Hermida – whose impressive culinary journey includes a stint in Asia working alongside Paul Pairet – delivers authentic modern cuisine that showcases carefully prepared seasonal ingredients. On the evening of our visit: peas with just a little bite, Bayonne ham and roasted hazelnuts to start, followed by medium rare fillet of veal, with aromatic basil and a delicate shallot tartlet.

Name: Chai Nous
Description: Set on a square in the Old Town of this picturesque village in the Cévennes foothills, this former wine bar has been taken over by a young couple. Maxime rustles up delightful dishes inspired by the local terroir, a case in point being his pâté en croûte of duck, foie gras and award-winning pork. Loann manages the restaurant floor with warmth and friendliness; her wine list features a selection of specialist winemakers. Terrace at the foot of the fountain. N.B. Pedestrian access only.

Name: Chai nous comme Chai vous
Address: 1 rue de la Garde, La Flotte, 17630, France
Description: (Temporarily closed) Friendly and attractive, this pocket handkerchief restaurant instantly makes you feel at home. The concise, appetising menu showcases island produce with a weakness for seafood, illustrated by the flawlessly cooked monkfish, flanked by a chardonnay-flavoured sabayon and white asparagus. Intelligently curated wine list, the occasional inventive note and a scattering of thoughtful attentions.

Name: Chante Bise
Description: In this restaurant with a festive and friendly atmosphere, Jackie and Christelle Flandin and team serve up their skilful and successfully modernised take on traditional cuisine. The lunch menu – presented verbally and served in the cosy and comfortable space – is full of shining examples: whiting and potato cromesquis served with a parsnip medley, or cabbage stuffed with braised cuttlefish, scallops and a braising jus infused with orange and passion fruit. The indulgence continues with the meticulously crafted desserts, such as a hazelnut and chocolate creation, highly nuanced in terms of both flavour and texture.

Name: Chantoiseau
Description: In 1765, Mathurin Roze de Chantoiseau opened the first modern restaurant (individual tables and dishes to choose from on a menu) in the Louvre area. In homage to him, brothers Nicolas and Julien Durand work in tandem to create lovely modern cuisine, which is also inspired by the French classics and occasionally makes use of noble products, as in the delicious puff pastry pigeon pie.

Name: Charbon Kunitoraya
Description: Outside, the attractive timber façade has a Japanese feel. Inside, you'll find an old zinc counter, Paris Métro-style tiling, mirrors, wood panelling, mouldings and two long solid wood tables. In this chic setting with a vintage feel, chef Nomoto – a pioneer of udon restaurants in France – serves up mainly multi-course tasting menus composed of traditional dishes, including poulet de Bresse yakitori, one of his specialities. Be sure to try one of the wagashi – traditional Japanese pastries that change with the seasons.

Name: Charbonnel
Description: An emblematic Périgord inn, situated in the very heart of the picturesque village of Brantôme. Comfortably seated in the dining room, which opens onto a pleasant terrace overlooking the River Dronne, diners tuck into delightful seasonal cuisine crafted from carefully sourced regional produce and peppered with exotic touches.

Name: Chardon
Description: The Chardon hosts chefs-in-residence, who temporarily take the helm and share a commitment to locally sourced ingredients. Each chef is given carte blanche for a single set menu. The result is fresh and succulent, served in a lovely bistro setting and paired with a fine selection of natural wines. Spot on!

Name: Chartron
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: Between the Drôme and Ardèche, this local landmark has been run by the Chartron family since 1946. Mathieu, the third generation, pursues the family legacy in a village famous for its Jean-Sébastien Bach Festival (July). The key to their success? Expertly crafted cuisine with quality ingredients: fillet of croaker with broad beans and leeks, grilled baby gem lettuce, wild garlic-spiked beurre blanc, or a strawberry delight of fruit compote and wild strawberry sorbet. They also offer a truffle menu in season together with a handful of cosy guestrooms.

Name: Chavant
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: In this enchanting family establishment, open since 1852, you can choose between a stylish dining room dripping in plush details (round, white tableclothed tables, silverware, coffered ceiling, wainscoting and a fireplace) or an idyllic alfresco terrace in fine weather. Chef Fabien Capogna crafts a savvily updated classical score, illustrated by crunchy, lacquered sweetbread, melt-in-the-mouth carrots, tangy seasoning and red port wine. Madame Chavant, who supervises the front-of-house, can be relied upon to greet each guest warmly and individually in line with the house motto: the customer is always right! The spacious guestrooms and pool may well entice you to stay longer…

Name: Chenapan
Description: The pair at the helm of this compact restaurant in Pigalle are chef Bruno Laporte and front-of-house manager and sommelier Florentin Fraillon, who have both graduated with honours from Ze Kitchen Galerie, William Ledeuil's "training ground"! Here, they are going from strength to strength, with dishes such as the plant-based starter (butter beans, fava beans, peas, leaves and fresh herbs) – given a boost by its rhubarb juice sauce spiced up with chilli in the style of a beurre blanc – or the delicious wheat dessert, oozing childhood nostalgia. An intimate, contemporary bistro setting with an open kitchen and pleasant service with a smile.

Name: Cheval Blanc
Description: In a building in the typical style of Sundgau, Alsace, food is a passion that has been handed down from generation to generation. Like his father before him, the chef cooks lovely traditional recipes with a modern edge, and has a particular penchant for game. Excellent wine selection.

Name: Chez Flo
Description: Guests are greeted with a smile in this friendly eatery… The same sunny disposition characterises the food, which is in the competent hands of an enthusiastic chef who changes his menu monthly. Uplifting, modern bistro fare composed with carefully selected ingredients: mild pepper from the Landes, Chalosse duck, Gastes saffron, Aquitaine peanuts… A first-rate dining experience, cheerful, seamless service and a lunchtime menu that won’t break the bank – what’s not to like?

Name: Chez Fonfon
Description: This family restaurant (1952) is pleasing in terms both of its contemporary interior and its seafood, freshly fished in the wooden pointu boats that can be seen bobbing about in the little port.

Name: Chez GN
Description: In an attractive building of honey-coloured Bordeaux stone, the young chef, who earned his stripes at Ursus in Tignes, Le Quatrième Mur and Le Logis de la Cadène, serves up his precise and creative bistronomy cuisine. Front of house, in the pared-back, refined setting with a veranda extension and garden, the chef's partner extends a warm welcome. The lunch set menu gives you two options; in the evening, choose between two set menus (without options). We particularly loved the pumpkin accompaniments to the ocean perch fillet: butternut squash risotto, creamy mousseline, cubes of Jack Be Little, tangy pickles and a delicious roasted seed paste, almost pistachio-like, all enhanced by a bright and delicate beurre blanc sauce. This is straightforward, delicious food, perfectly seasoned and impeccably executed.

Name: Chez Jean - La Métairie Dupont
Description: The Dupont family estate is enjoying its new lease of life. Antoine, scrum-half for the French national rugby team, and Clément, a Noir de Bigorre pig farmer, have taken over the property purchased by their grandparents in the 1960s. Expect authenticity, terroir and family spirit. The pork is prepared in a variety of ways – it might be finely cured, the offal slow-cooked, the loin pan-fried or even used as a filling for devilled eggs. Be sure to try the duck breast in a casserole, from an iconic recipe handed down by the grandfather. A buzzing atmosphere on the restaurant floor, smiling staff and South-Western character.

Name: Chez Loustic
Description: In one of the busiest parts of the Saint-Cyprien neighbourhood, this modern bistro has an industrial aesthetic that makes for a convivial atmosphere. The pleasant little terrace overlooking the square is a bonus. Having learned the ropes at a Christian Constant restaurant, the chef prepares meticulous seasonal cuisine using market-fresh produce.

Name: Chez Marie en Corse
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Founded by Marie Orsini, this family-run guesthouse continues to thrive under the stewardship of her nephew Pascal, in partnership with chef Sergio Risdonne. The premises also house a bar, tobacconist and Italian-Corsican delicatessen, plus a few rooms for overnight stays. Entry is via the bar terrace, then the shop, with its terrazzo flooring; at the rear is a shaded, bucolic terrace with wrought-iron tables and greenery. The concise menu proposes traditional Italian cuisine that is bursting with freshness: imported artisanal pasta, Corsican charcuterie in the sauces – think mezzi rigatoni alla carbonara with bulagna. Seasonal specials and the catch of the day are also available.

Name: Chez Mathilde
Description: Mathilde is the daughter of Eric Jacquier, the legendary guardian of Lake Geneva’s fishing traditions. She has set up shop in this cheerful eatery in the heart of the village with a concrete counter, a glimpse of the kitchen through the hatch, off-kilter lighting, light wood bistro furnishings and a spacious shaded patio. Her concise slate menu resembles her spontaneous, playful and intuitive personality and stars local produce like fish from the lake (whitefish, Arctic char, etc.) and veg from small growers. We warrant you too will fall in love with its feel-good vibe!

Name: Chez Mattin
Description: This building, characteristic of the local area, is delightfully rustic, with its wooden tables and exposed beams, and has a real family atmosphere. Basque specialities and market-based daily specials make for lively cuisine that never fails to surprise: txangurro (specialities based on spider crab meat), ttoro (fish soup), txipirones (baby squid). Fish takes pride of place and it is exceptionally good!

Name: Chez Michel
Description: Since 2015, Japanese chef Masahiro Kawai has been in charge of the kitchens at this restaurant steeped in history. He draws on his experience in Japan, Spain and France (working with Yves Camdeborde and Christian Etchebest) to create traditional yet cheerful bistro cuisine, in which seafood ingredients play a key role. The classics are present and correct – roast foie gras, game in season – the flavours are delicious and the cooking is precise, particularly in the case of the grilled mackerel, ratatouille and pistou.

Name: Chez Mimi
Address: 3 bis place du Général-Leclerc, Colombes, 92700, France
Description: In the heart of Colombes, close to the imposing church designed by Jean Hébrard, this place started out as a brasserie in 1907. With its zinc counter, mirrors, ceiling mouldings and chandelier with white globes, the decor is truly eye-catching and makes for a chic setting in which to enjoy traditional cuisine prepared with care and made with quality produce. The menu includes a number of signature dishes, such as veal chop or beef fillet..

Name: Chez Mon Jules
Description: In Drôme provençale, the cheerful mismatched interior sports a patchwork of paraphernalia (typewriters, weighing scales, disco balls and a self-service vinyl turntable). The single set menu features cherry-picked, mainly organic produce with a weakness for veg, but not only. An example: rack of lamb paired with wild garlic and a date, cumin and garlic seasoning. Panoramic terrace and four quaint guestrooms to wind down and relax in style.

Name: Chez Monsieur
Description: This is the archetypal Parisian bistro in all its glory (zinc countertop, dark red velvet banquette seating, mirrors, patterned tiles), with the classic – and delicious! – bistro cuisine that goes with it: onion soup with a Comté topping, veal blanquette served in an individual cocotte, veal kidneys with wholegrain mustard, crêpes Suzette. To go with the food, a wide selection of wines from all over France.

Name: Chez Mosse
Description: The boss here is Mattéo Mosse, a youthful chef from Haute Savoie who decided to settle in this village to be as close as possible to the countryside and to small local producers. Fish and meat from sustainable breeders, as local as possible and a vegetarian score depict the ethos of this eco-responsible eatery. The chef’s modern repertory unsurprisingly revolves around seasonal produce, with a distinct weakness for organic veggies. A simple, no-fuss bistro interior in a colourful village house that is flanked by a refreshingly shady terrace.

Name: Chez Parenti
Description: Chez Parenti has been passed down through generations of the same family since 1935! Lovers of impeccably fresh seafood are in for a treat – lobster and crayfish sold by weight, fish caught in the bay… and a selection of Corsican meats ensures there's something for everyone. The meal ends on a high note with the restaurant's signature Crêpe Suzette, flambéed tableside. The dishes are perfectly cooked and skilfully put together. Enjoy this culinary experience in the comfort of the large shaded terrace that faces the Gulf of Valinco and the boats at anchor.

Name: Chez Pimousse
Description: Pierre-Michaël Martin, otherwise known as "Pimousse", has set up shop on Quai Saint-Vincent, overlooking Vieux Lyon and the River Saône. The light-filled dining room is reminiscent of a country villa, with its old wooden tables, classic bistro chairs, dried grasses and wooden bar. He greets regulars with a smile, occasionally even pitching in with the service. He wins diners over with his meticulously crafted dishes and surprise menus, based on impeccably fresh top-notch produce. Think John Dory fillet, peas and asparagus with pickled berries and a creamy smoked pike roe sauce. In fine weather, don't miss the lovely terrace beneath the plane trees.

Name: Chez Romuald
Description: The wide glass façade of this modern building affords a glimpse into the light-filled interior, which features an exposed brick wall and touches of greenery. The chef turns out precise, unpretentious cuisine, in which the premium ingredients speak for themselves. Raw scallops are cut into thick slices and served in their shells, enhanced with a dill-orange vinaigrette, plus a lemon gel for added freshness and complexity. More rooted in local tradition, the farm-reared Landes chicken is incredibly tender, with a sweet potato purée and a rich, reduced jus. Confidently executed, well-balanced dishes that reflect true culinary craftsmanship, with a clear focus on flavour.

Name: Chez Rémi
Description: Sporting his checked shirt and blue apron, Rémi officiates behind what was likely the counter of this former betting shop, which has been turned into a cosy little bistro. On the menu for lunch today: a tasty chicken liver terrine; redfish bream with its delicious fumet; poached peach, financier and creamy house-made vanilla ice cream. One of the major draws is the restaurant's friendly atmosphere. Photos of the chef and his past co-workers adorn the walls, and a blackboard features the day's set menus. Customers collect their wine from the wine cellar, whether to accompany their meal here or to take home. Welcome to Rémi's!

Name: Chez Suzanne
Description: An appealingly accessible take on fine dining! Chef Julien Poisot (previously at Château de Mercuès) and his partner Justine run this restaurant at one end of the Pont Valentré – a magnificent medieval bridge. As simple in its presentation as it is sophisticated in its execution, this generous cuisine showcases the chef's experience in the form of delicious, meticulous dishes inspired by seasonal produce. The lunch menu is just as down to earth (mackerel with white wine and horseradish cream; stuffed Gascon pork and ​​brioche perdue). In the evening, the chef draws on premium ingredients to create more elaborate options (eg gilthead bream, oyster mushrooms, leek soubise, shellfish sauce).

Name: Chez Séraphin
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Great view,Terrace
Description: A characteristic Corsican house in a charming mountainside village sets the splendid scene to sample wholesome country fare, prepared simply from painstakingly selected ingredients, among which Corsica’s famous cured meats and fruit, vegetables and herbs from the garden. Take a seat on the spacious terrace and drink in the jaw-dropping view of the mountains and ancient oak forest. Just a word of warning: bank cards are not accepted, so take cash!

Name: Chez Éric
Description: On the square of a charming village, this dry-stone building has everything you could wish for from a shaded patio to a vaulted interior with limewashed walls and a wood-burning fireplace – ideal to sample the black truffle menu in season. The chef rolls out big-boned Provençal fare rich in gutsy flavours, depicted by chunks of monkfish in a saffron-spiked stew. Gracious front-of-house service and well-curated wine list.

Name: Chocho
Description: In this buzzy establishment that is invariably packed to the seams, Franco-American chef Thomas Chisholm, a former Top Chef contestant, celebrates sharing and sustainable fine dining. You can expect ikejime fish, rows of jars and fermentations and agroforestry ingredients… His creative, sometimes playful culinary style is skilfully blended with globetrotting influences: orange glazed sand carrots, cream of sunflower and kumquat preserves; scallops and raw foie gras flanked by a stock of roast celeriac perfumed in soy sauce, lemon grass and galanga…

Name: Choral
Description: In the Romains district, a 10-min walk from the centre, take a seat in this cosy dining room, decked in a clever blend of Japanese minimalism and Scandinavian design codes. The repertory stars healthy, hearty seasonal dishes made with cherry-picked produce: the last wax beans of the season sautéed in almond cream, sorrel, tarragon and parmesan; pearlescent medallions of Breton monkfish, paired with hispi cabbage and a fishbone stock laced with ginger and lemon grass; without forgetting their legendary Cuban chocolate tart – to die for! Natural wine list and other artisanal beverages.

Name: Château Grand Barrail
Address: Route de Libourne D243, Saint-Emilion, 33330, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: This neo-Romantic château built in 1902 lies in the heart of the Saint-Émilion vineyards. It blends a time-honoured setting with contemporary design and diners sit either in the Art Nouveau-inspired lounges or on the beautiful terrace that looks out over the grounds and a sea of vines. At lunchtime, bistronomy dishes such as crispy duck, finely puréed sweet potato and roasted hazelnuts are served. The dinner menu features more ambitious cuisine (roasted veal sweetbreads with Bordeaux butter, a medley of carrots and their tops, cardamom jus).

Name: Château Hochberg
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The restaurant set within an imposing 19C residence unveils a trendy decor dotted with creations by master glassmaker René Lalique (whose museum is just opposite). The chef concocts succulent seasonal cuisine inspired by the Alsace and Vosges terroir: goose foie gras terrine, gravlax of Sparsbach trout, steak with maitre d’ beurre and crunchy polenta. Lovely terrace to the rear of the chateau overlooking the grounds.

Name: Château de Rochecotte
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A hop from the Bourgueil vineyards, this elegant château dating back to the Enlightenment and set in sumptuous grounds puts on a gourmet-friendly culinary performance. Whether it is in the trendy conservatory overlooking lush countryside, in the classically appointed dining room or alfresco in the shade of a massive cedar tree, you will sample deftly-crafted Gallic staples with a modern twist.

Name: Château du Bost
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A few minutes from Vichy, in peaceful grounds, this château with towers and a water-filled moat (15C-19C) offers a contemporary and cosy decor, complemented by a beautiful terrace and some comfortable guestrooms. The restaurant has a refined setting and serves tasty seasonal cuisine.

Name: Chère Amie
Address: 5 avenue de la Marseillaise, Strasbourg, 67000, France
Description: In the Neustadt district, the former Hôtel des Postes – a monumental Prussian building – has undergone a complete renovation. The name ("Dear Friend") and decor of this spacious brasserie are inspired by letter writing… but rather a love note or a business letter? The choice is yours! Peruse the carefully devised menu of traditional dishes such as sauerkraut, beef tartare, bouchée à la reine, beef tenderloin with Bordelaise sauce, fish terrine and lobster bisque. A contemporary setting and good value for money – definitely something to write home about!

Name: Ciasa Mia
Description: In a side street near the Pantheon, this charming little restaurant with exposed stone walls and wooden furnishings has a rustic feel that calls to mind a chalet. At the helm is an Italian couple in their forties: he is in charge in the kitchen, she takes care of proceedings front of house, dressed in the traditional attire of the Dolomites. The food is presented in surprise set menus, in which an inventive spin is put on local ingredients and bitter flavours are subtly explored – a hallmark of refined Italian cuisine. A good selection of wines completes the experience.

Name: Ciel à Table
Description: On the church square in this village in the Toulouse Conurbation, this typical pink brick building has now been extended by a large room with a glass roof and a patio shaded by a chestnut tree and a lime tree. The light-filled restaurant room boasts contemporary decor and a large open kitchen. The cuisine reflects the style of the place, flirting with the zeitgeist, in dishes such as Mediterranean tuna bao with notes of sesame, or pigeon served two ways: the leg confit and the supreme cooked whole. Attentive and alert service.

Name: Circus
Description: A young couple from the region – Nino on the savoury side, Salomé handling desserts and service – cultivate a wine-bistro atmosphere in this former crêperie; a natural fit for this wine-growing town! Their cooking rooted in meticulously sourced produce is both fresh and indulgent: think Jura snails, charcoal-grilled oyster mushrooms and Brussels sprouts; house-made agnoletti, potatoes, Bleu de la Marre cheese in an oxidative wine sauce; bergamot, sweetcorn and yuzu sorbet… A lovely little spot.

Name: Citrus
Description: This restaurant in a traditional old building with a pretty patio to be enjoyed on sunny days has a small lemon-yellow dining area (echoing the name Citron) with exposed stone walls and modern bistro furniture. Éric Sampietro (previously chef at La Table des Cordeliers) concocts appealingly hearty fare, from vegetable broth with pork dumpling to roasted pear with ginger caramel, crumble and yoghurt ice cream.

Name: Claire et Hugo
Address: 77 avenue du Général-Galliéni, à Sainte-Savine, Troyes, 10300, France
Description: An enthusiastic self-taught young couple runs this restaurant with a subdued decor composed of raw materials. The premises also house a bakery and delicatessen leading onto a lovely terrace and indoor garden (including a citrus tree greenhouse). The ingredients, which are 95% organic, make for healthy, tasty and balanced dishes.

Name: Clos d'Astorg
Description: "Cuisine au beurre" on the façade lets you know what to expect – butter is central to the recipes); "chou farci" reveals the house speciality: generously portioned, packed with a soft, light and fragrant farce, wrapped in a delicate green cabbage leaf. The interior is also done out in a bistro vein: mosaic and hardwood floors, exposed stone and brick walls, white tablecloths and light wood chairs. The confident cuisine focuses on the essentials, with leek vinaigrette, egg mayonnaise or green asparagus with mousseline sauce. Meat lovers are spoiled for choice: breaded veal sweetbreads "meunière", onglet steak with Bleu de Bresse cheese, boudin noir. And those with a sweet tooth are catered for with chocolate mousse, hazelnut and caramel riz au lait.

Name: Clover Grill
Description: Mouthwatering dry - aged meats – Baltic black beef, Bavarian beef, Blonde d'Aquitaine, Black Angus – take pride of place in the window, drawing in diners keen to try them for themselves. From the starters to the desserts, everything is cooked over coals or roasted on a spit, giving the dining experience its own particular flavour. A great success.

Name: Clovis
Description: This bistro in the heart of a medieval village has a short menu with an original concept: several starter + main course pairings built around a flagship ingredient, such as a vegetable, Mediterranean fish or meat, often Parthenaise beef from the family farm in Vendée. We recommend starting with an aperitif and charcuterie. Warm welcome; excellent wine list. Adjacent to the restaurant is a wine bar, which serves delicious platters.

Name: Clovis & Basina
Description: In a picturesque hilltop village in the Vaucluse, this stone building used to house a bakery. In summer, tables are laid out on a delightful terrace in the shade of a mulberry tree, overlooking the vineyards and Mt Ventoux. Inside, terracotta floor tiles, whitewashed walls and a large communal table make for a charming dining experience in winter. Every month, the concise menu changes, showcasing modern Provençal cuisine through fragrant, well-seasoned dishes, such as a beautiful pairing of tomato with Parmesan and panisse, or peach and apricot combined in an indulgent dessert. A spot that exudes sunshine.

Name: Clutch
Description: In a setting emblematic of modern-day, trendy Eastern Paris (full-length picture windows, rough stone walls, bistro tables, an open kitchen and a few seats at the counter), the accent is on creative bistronomic fare, peppered with Asian notes. Casual, bouncy vibe.

Name: Clément Artisan Cuisinier
Description: In the heart of Pujols, a few kilometres from Villeneuve-sur-Lot, Clément Papillaud has established a refined dining spot in a traditional building with thick stone walls and whitewashed beams. It comprises two dining rooms, a bar area with club chairs, and a lovely, peaceful terrace. Drawing on a career that has taken him from the Plaza Athénée to La Table du Marensin, the chef devises straightforward dishes with bold flavours underpinned by meticulous local sourcing – for example, tender and juicy Cantal pork belly topped with an umeboshi and furikake paste, served with a black sesame jus, courtesy of one of France's few producers of the seeds, Philippe Guichard in Pailloles.

Name: Cocagne
Address: 26 avenue de la Liberté, Autignac, 34480, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
Description: This intimate restaurant featuring a counter around the open kitchen is tucked away to the rear of Château Autignac, right in the heart of the Faugères AOP. Fabien Lefebvre (Meilleur Ouvrier de France) cooks up Mediterranean cuisine inspired by the market and enhanced with Catalan, Moroccan and Japanese influences. Sommelier Rachel Lefebvre curates the wine pairings. The tonnato vitello – barbecued Mediterranean bluefin tuna – sets the tone, and is followed by premium Sisteron lamb, lemon harissa and panoufle kebab, with a herbaceous and refreshing dessert with chocolate and green Chartreuse rounding off the meal. This delightful menu is composed entirely of local produce, and dishes are plated in front of guests, making for a convivial atmosphere. Warm welcome included.

Name: Colbert
Description: In a modern brasserie setting, the chef rustles up traditional flavoursome food that spans the full gamut of classic French cuisine: eggs meurette, house smoked salmon, vol au vent and Simmental hanger steak with marrow bone… Given the quality of the food, it is hardly surprising that the restaurant is frequently fully booked.

Name: Colibri
Address: 14 rue de la Mittrie, Dinan, 22100, France
Description: In the heart of medieval Dinan, this modern bistro sports wood furnishings, oak parquet flooring, a fireplace and a view of the kitchen from the dinky dining room. Vibrant, often surf ‘n turf recipes set the culinary scene: lobster, green peas and strawberries, mullet, black pudding and figs; raspberries, red pepper sorbet and chiffon cake…

Name: Colita
Description: Located between Nice's port and the Colline du Château, this restaurant brings together the flavours of Colombia and Italy in bright and colourful fusion dishes cooked up by chefs Carlos and Daniele. Diners soak up the warm, relaxed atmosphere on the spacious terrace with orange seating or in the narrow indoor dining space done out in terracotta hues. In the visible kitchen, it is all about open-flame cooking – on plancha and parrilla grills. Grilled octopus, braised veal chop and sardines in a chimichurri sauce deliver intense flavours; a vibrant and well-balanced Peruvian ceviche combines white fish, red onion, crunchy sweetcorn and sweet potato. An authentic spot straddling two culinary cultures.

Name: Colvert
Description: This bistro in the picturesque Latin Quarter of Paris boasts a bubbly vibe, vintage charm and bold, deftly crafted cuisine whose hearty Gallic twang is treated to dollop of creative enthusiasm. Stellar technique and a quest for flavour are expressed in stuffed squid, roast Mallard duck and plum clafoutis illustrate the. Attentive service, nostalgic recipes with a twist and a bona fide Parisian bistro décor!

Name: Comme Chez Maman
Description: This contemporary bistro near a green square in the heart of the Batignolles neighbourhood is a real home from home. The Belgian chef, Wim Van Gorp, makes lovely contemporary dishes that he peppers with creative touches, and some of which pay delicious tribute to his Flemish roots.

Name: Complices
Description: An eye for detail and a passion for precision set the scene for fresh, no-nonsense cuisine rustled up by the duo formed by Hugo and Sophie, respectively in charge of savoury dishes and desserts. This couple of well-travelled chefs, who honed their skills in starred establishments, creates dishes that revolve around local seasonal produce, sometimes enhanced by exotic seasonings. A few examples: duck foie gras with smoked eel and a yuzu ponzu sauce, or black Bigorre pork paired with turnip-rooted chervil, tamarind gel, coffee and citron. The feast continues with Sophie's delicious, on-point desserts.

Name: Comptoir du Marché
Description: In the heart of bustling historic Nice, casual and friendly are the watchwords of this vintage-inspired market counter, whose name is equal to the chef’s colourful, flavoursome dishes. Concise menu, unfailingly fresh and reasonable rates: it is always a pleasure to spend time here.

Name: Comète
Address: 35 rue de la Grève, Saint-Lunaire, 35800, France
Description: Bang in the middle of the seaside resort, not far from the beach, this bistro has a no-frills, old-school decor: old pine floorboards, mismatched second-hand furniture, vintage-style light fittings. Chef Victor Nicolas rustles up creative dishes starring top-notch ingredients, underpinned by simple yet effective preparations, elegant sauces and punchy condiments.

Name: Confins des Sens
Description: The house speciality is a delicious muscat-flavoured foie gras soup with a confit of red onions and ‘cromesquis’. The chefs pay tribute to the region whilst respecting the seasons, illustrated by a velvety soup of green peas and an ice cream of fresh cow’s cheese flavoured with wild garlic. Other highlights include pork cheeks braised in a local red wine or free-range chicken wings stuffed with morels and flanked by “pressed” potatoes (finely sliced and stacked before being roasted). The terrace is glorious in the sunshine.

Name: Coretta
Description: In the Clichy-Batignolles district, opposite Martin Luther King Park (King's wife was called Coretta), Mexican-born chef Beatriz Gonzalez, with stints in star-rated eateries of the likes of Senderens and La Grande Cascade, consummately curates a season-driven menu rich in big-boned generous flavours. Youthful, buzzy front-of-house team and a bright airy designer interior overlooking the trees in the park from the second floor.

Name: Coup de Main
Description: Victor Berthe (previously at Rozó) and Clément Delécluse (France's Young Sommelier of 2021) have set up shop in the heart of the Saint-André neighbourhood in Vieux Lille. With good humour, the two partners welcome diners to their compact little restaurant and wine shop with an open kitchen and vintage furnishings. The short menu sets the tone: starters for sharing, a choice between fish, meat and a vegetarian main, and just two desserts. For dinner, there's also a tasting menu that brilliantly combines seasonal dishes with playful and varied cuisine based on ingredients from small-scale producers, with whom the duo maintain close ties. Natural wine list.

Name: Couvert de Vignes
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Montagne de Reims, this restaurant is helmed by Benjamin Gilles, who signs a modern repertory packed in fresh flavours and enhanced by a zest of creativity. Vegetables and fruit feature prominently in his culinary score through a variety of preparations (raw, cooked, pickled).

Name: Crustum
Description: On their premises on the market square, Axel Folastre and Céline Mention have brought their vision to life: a bright space with an arty decor and a delicatessen display case (pâté en croûte, foie gras, pies etc). Together, they cook up personal and precise cuisine, their balanced dishes demonstrating authentic expertise – the beef fillet is cooked to perfection and enhanced by a fine marriage of oysters, lemon and fennel. On the restaurant floor, too, they work as a team. Céline crafts the desserts with equal parts skill and heart.

Name: Crêperie Grain Noir
Address: 16 rue de la Herse, Saint-Malo, 35400, France
Description: Opposite the Halle au Blé in Saint-Malo, this little crêperie is not to be missed. It serves classic galettes (buckwheat pancakes), as well as more original recipes: the "langouille" galette is with pork tongue; the "Grain Noir" with Breton trout, fresh goat's cheese, crunchy vegetables and lemon; the "Ty Nevez" with andouille from Dinan, egg, Emmental and mustard. They also serve hors d'oeuvre, such as chilli butter and raw cocoa nibs, and salted butter and seaweed tartar. Most of the ingredients are organic; the ciders and wines are natural.

Name: Cueillette
Description: A small establishment tucked away in the Rennes suburbs, with an inviting façade, a contemporary interior, a covered terrace overlooking the fields, and a charming welcome. At the helm, Armand and Fanny form a close-knit duo, working in perfect harmony to delight their guests. The chef has it all figured out: his cuisine – streamlined, delicate, and executed flawlessly – features clever pairings and spot-on seasoning. At lunchtime, a budget-friendly set menu makes this lovely urban spot even more irresistible.

Name: Cuisine-à-Manger
Address: Hôtel L'Ermitage, chemin de l'Ermitage, Saint-Cyr-au-Mont-d'Or, 69450, France
Description: The restaurant of this hotel perched on Mt Cindre overlooks the Monts du Lyonnais and the city, taking in a sweeping panorama. The kitchen follows the market without ever getting stuck on repeat, serving generous, expertly turned dishes, such as Castilian red pork palomita with piperade vegetables and a chorizo emulsion. The desserts are even bolder: chocolate with smoked vanilla ice cream, balsamic reduction and black garlic, or strawberry pavlova with celery-lemon sorbet.

Name: Cuq en Terrasses
FacilitiesAndServices: Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: Perched high in the village, this charming 18C house is a haven of calm, whose unusual, terraced grounds showcase the produce of the kitchen garden. The restaurant is helmed by two young professionals with stints in starred establishments in Toulouse under their belt, who concoct delicate seasonal cuisine: gratin of artichoke with aromatic herbs and a chorizo emulsion; river trout from Condax fish farm and almond stuffing. The view of the Lauragais plain and the Pyrenees from the conservatory and terrace is breathtaking. Extend the experience in this tranquil setting in one of the charming guestrooms.

Name: Curnonsky
Description: Chef Benjamin Capelier is back at the helm of this restaurant that he already ran once before. Renamed Curnonsky in homage to the famous food critic and his first restaurant in Lyon, the establishment remains true to its original spirit: a wallet-friendly single set menu for lunch and a multi-course tasting experience at dinner. In a very simple and convivial setting, this discreet and focused chef delivers delicious modern cuisine, with each dish reflecting meticulous attention to texture and flavour. He is passionate about wine (an understatement) and recommends the perfect pairings himself from an exceptional wine list at wine merchant prices.

Name: Cypsèle
Description: Two partners with an impressive international pedigree have opened this ambitious restaurant on Île Saint-Louis: chef Marcin Król, who has worked at Noma, Oaxen Krog, Borago and Le Chateaubriand, and sommelier Quentin Loisel, previously at Jules Verne, who has curated a remarkable wine list. The concept: a surprise menu that changes daily, composed according to the day's fresh produce. This spontaneity makes for pure, unadulterated flavours. The chef's take on market-driven cuisine is less about technical prowess than the effortless harmony of the pairings; creative without going overboard, the dishes are characterised by finely tuned seasoning and a command of wood-fired cooking, both in the oven and over a robatayaki-style barbecue. Redesigned by a fashionable design studio, the decor is a blend of historical heritage and contemporary elements: 18C wooden shelf fronts, neon lighting, a gradient mosaic and sleek oak furniture.

Name: Cécile
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the lively, bustling Carmes neighbourhood, a close-knit young team welcomes you to this modern bistro with a wood-decked veranda, large open kitchen and contemporary decor. The short menu is inspired by a real mix of cultures: exotic touches are incorporated into dishes such as Thai duck tartare and farm-reared pork loin with mango and pomegranate.

Name: Céna
