The set menu showcases local produce from the lakes (arctic char), rivers (crayfish) and forests (game in season), without forgetting forays to Italy (Piedmont hazelnut gnocchi and Colonnata bacon). A fine dining experience starring tasty modern cuisine with a knockout view of Mont Blanc to boot - what’s not to like?

Name: La Ferme de Voisins
Description: You reach this lovely 19C farmhouse via a flower-decked courtyard, which serves as a patio in summertime. The relatively concise menu shines the spotlight on the house classics, which are prawns on sticks, the ‘irreplaceable’ calf’s head and signature desserts such as the rum and orange punch baba, together with a range of tasty and creative dishes. A fine establishment to try out post-haste!

Name: La Ferme du Chozal
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: The restaurant may sport a characteristic rustic Alpine vibe, but the appetising cuisine is no less modern, made with fine local ingredients. And let's not forget the remarkable list of Alpine wines.

Name: La Ferme du Pré
Address: Route de Suresnes - Bois de Boulogne, Paris, 75016, France
Description: In a characteristic Normandy-style outbuilding, just opposite his restaurant Le Pré Catelan, chef and Meilleur Ouvrier de France Frédéric Anton fetes bistro classics, with simple, generous dishes such as boudin noir, chou farci, skate wing with beurre blanc, and profiteroles. The long narrow dining area with exposed ceiling beams exudes rustic charm with its vintage decor and old-fashioned crockery. A delightful terrace shaded by the trees of the Bois de Boulogne.

Name: La Fine Bouche
Description: The chef's interest in regional traditions and his creative spirit are reflected in his use of the capuchin, an ancient utensil with a cast iron cone attached to a long rod, in which pieces of bacon are melted and used to flambée his scallops, lending them a slight grilled and smoked taste. With its hardwood floors, mouldings and exposed stonework, the tastefully refurbished dining room makes for an intimate dinner setting.

Name: La Fine Fourchette
Address: 2500 avenue du Bugey, à Virignin, Belley, 01300, France
Description: A jaw-dropping view over the Canal du Rhône and an elegant interior set the scene in this renowned regional temple of good food. Generous portions of Ain produce take the limelight in the chef’s well-crafted score, depicted by fascinating flavour combinations and impeccable plating. Special mention for the strawberry-themed dessert that will knock the tastebuds off fans of fine French fare!

Name: La Flamiche
Description: A classical interior lies behind the large windows of La Flamiche. Here, cuisine with robust traditional foundations is enhanced by a touch of modernity: one example would be the duck foie gras and smoked trout in a Granny Smith jelly, cucumber pickles and apple chutney – a beautifully crafted starter. Then there are the medallions of monkfish with lime, carrot and rocket, perfectly cooked in butter, the good old-fashioned way.

Name: La Fleur de Sel
Description: This spruce family-run business en route to the ski resorts is eminently welcoming. The several-course menu respects the seasons and showcases the cornucopia of excellent Savoyard produce. Cosy and fashionable, the interior also sports a warm rustic edge courtesy of a fireplace insert in the centre of the room. A lovely alfresco terrace adds to the establishment’s appeal.

Name: La Flèche d'Argent
Address: Hôtel Princesse Flore, 5 place Allard, Royat, 63130, France
Description: The name, La Flèche d'Argent, is a nod to the iconic ‘Silver Arrows’ Mercedes-Benz racing cars of the 1930s and to the nearby Charade automobile racetrack. In a smart decor, chef Clément Lorente signs expertly crafted cuisine with an up-to-the-minute creative twang in several-course set menus. The ingredients are of the highest quality: foie gras from the Plaine de Limagne, trout from Corrèze, saffron from Mazayes, pigeon from Dombes. The house dessert, a tribute to the chef's grandmother's Agen prune flan, is flambéed tableside and is a guaranteed showstopper. Simpler set menu at lunchtime; brunch on Sundays.

Name: La Fontaine - L’Artiste et le Cuisinier
Description: This trendy bistro nestles in an attractive old house tucked away in a narrow street of an eminently Instagrammable village. A couple (he is the cook and she is the artist) invites us to sample their bistronomic handiwork tinted by wanderlust and inspired by the bold flavours of locally sourced seasonal produce.

Name: La Forge
Address: 1 rue de la Brosse, Le Subdray, 18570, France
Description: This restaurant run by a sincere and welcoming couple in an old farmhouse about 15km from Bourges is definitely one to recommend. Everything is house-made, most of the vegetables come from the family's own garden, and freshness is the order of the day in each dish. Multi-course set menus – more elaborate in the evening and at weekends – to be enjoyed on the shaded terrace bordered by the garden.

Name: La Forge
Description: Fontaine-Daniel is the epitome of an old French country village and the birthplace of the famous Toiles de Mayenne fabrics. Overlooking a pond and the forest, this venue is housed in a former outbuilding of a Cistercian abbey, which became the hub of this textile manufacturing enterprise in the 19C. Chef William Blondel cooks primarily with local produce that he doesn’t hesitate to enhance with modern and creative twists gleaned from his own globetrotting travels.

Name: La Foucaudière
Address: 2 place de la Foucaudière, Senillé-Saint-Sauveur, 86100, France
Description: This quiet restaurant on the outskirts of Châtellerault features a minimalist decor in a palette of sandy hues. In the kitchen, Richard Robe demonstrates his experience – his perfectly balanced dishes reveal strong technical skills: crispy tempura frogs' legs, home-made ketchup and herb pesto; free-range chicken grilled flat on the yakitori barbecue, served with sauce diable; vanilla and buckwheat caramel millefeuille. Generous food that exudes sincerity.

Name: La Fourchette
Description: In the historic city centre, this warm and lively bistro wins diners over with its smiling welcome and convivial atmosphere – and is frequently full. The traditional cuisine, rooted in the South of France, focuses on well-executed, comforting dishes: white pudding, breaded pig's trotters with mustard, veal onglet with mustard sauce and pommes dauphine, Avignon-style beef daube… and a praline meringue glacée, a special suggested that day by the waitstaff. An unpretentious and indulgent family-run restaurant.

Name: La Gaffe
Description: Chef Yann Le Scavarec, who hails from Morbihan, is at the helm of this restaurant, which boasts an ideal location on the Saint-Florent harbour front. His well-crafted contemporary cooking showcases local produce, eg lamb and veal from Oletta, fish sourced directly from a local fisherman, barbecued crayfish. Try the bluefin tuna, puffed rice crust, served as a tartare with nori, miso-cooked aubergine and a sesame and lime condiment. The elegant modern interior reflects the philosophy behind the food.

Name: La Galupe
Description: Moored on the banks of the Adour, this former bargemen's inn is said to be over three centuries old. It still proudly boasts its spruce white façade with the characteristic red shutters of the Basque Country and an interior with its cachet intact – stone flooring, exposed beams and an open fireplace. Even the original fish counter and the hooks for drying the fish are still present and correct. This restaurant, which for 30 years was run by famous Basque chef Christian Parra, now has Stéphane Besse at the helm. Very local ingredients are the foundation of his fresh, colourful cuisine; the fishermen, duck and lamb farmers, the baker, the ceramist (who designed the plates) are all from the village.

Name: La Gare
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: A very contemporary local institution (since 1874)! It has a perfect combination of elegance, vitality and conviviality, offering a brasserie for those in a hurry or carefully-prepared modern cuisine in a conservatory setting... all accompanied by one of the finest wine lists in the country.

Name: La Garenne
Address: Le Dracy, 4 rue du Pressoir, Dracy-le-Fort, 71640, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: An appealing place where you can enjoy, for example, a venison and foie gras pâté en croute with pickled vegetables and gherkin condiment, or a lobster-stuffed veal tournedos, with conchiglie and mushrooms. The contemporary-style dining room, with glass-fronted wine cellar, overlooks the terrace and grounds. The hotel, meanwhile, boasts pleasant guestrooms, a swimming pool and a spa.

Name: La Gloire
Description: A venerable Montargis institution, located alongside the N7. For several generations, culinary tradition has been revisited with flair and generosity; do not miss out on the rather imposing dessert trolley.

Name: La Golmotte
Description: Not far from Le Mont-Dore, authenticity is guaranteed in this inn, whose dining room was once a cowshed! Fresh ingredients and hearty portions of wholesome traditional fare, such as scallops in a sauce vierge, calf’s sweetbread with morels, or blueberry-flavoured crème brûlée. The warm, heartfelt welcome is as genuine as the score is big-boned and rustic. Remember to book!

Name: La Gourmandière
Description: A longstanding Ardennes institution, this plush 1890 property is enjoying a new lease of life courtesy of two young brothers-cum-partners. The deftly plated dishes slalom between tradition and modernity: pressed foie gras laced in old rum, veal sweetbread, Rossini tournedos steak, turbot and risotto of fregola sarda… Gloriously peaceful patio to the rear.

Name: La Grande Brasserie BIB
Description: In the heart of Avignon, in a fine historical building – once a cloister – Mathieu Desmarest (Pollen) has swapped bistronomy for this brasserie, which is open seven days a week. The focus is on traditional French cuisine: devilled eggs, pâté en croûte, Burgundy snails or andouillette with mustard sauce, plus a weekly special (eg confit duck parmentier with aioli). Three concepts under one roof: brasserie, cocktail and tapas bar, and cheese bar. For fine weather, the leafy terrace in the courtyard is one of the city's loveliest spots.

Name: La Grande Georgette
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The name is a nod to an amusing tradition whereby a fire engine’s ladder was named after the captain's wife. In the former Chanzy fire station (1926), chef Julien Raphanel crafts a high-flying score: lightly seared langoustine with a briny seaweed sabayon; pan-fried Racan pigeon, caramelised apples and buckwheat espuma… The terrace commands a jaw-dropping view of Reims cathedral. Next-door, Little Georgette rolls out a bistronomic lineup of French family favourites at reasonable prices.

Name: La Grande Salle
Address: Hôtel de France, place de la Libération, Auch, 32000, France
Description: Revamped from top to toe, this city-centre institution is still going strong under the aegis of a family team, namely three brothers – one in the dining room (an MOF), one in the kitchen and one is a pastry chef! The culinary lineup aims to highlight the gastronomic heritage of the Gers region: raw and cooked scallops; Bigorre black pork and leeks; duck and foie gras pie, sliced at the table; baked Alaska, flambéed in front of you! Foodies with an appetite will be delighted to learn that the sauce boats are left on the table – irresistible with the house made bread! Simpler fare at Le 9ème brasserie.

Name: La Grange
Description: This former barn is now an inviting country chic restaurant appointed in an alpine vein. The menu stars tasty well-crafted food, made with premium regional ingredients such as marinated salmon trout from Lake Oô; confit of egg, shredded confit of duck and creamy sweetcorn… What’s not to like?

Name: La Grange
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A wood-rich interior and a striking feeding trough set the scene in this isolated old farmstead that is clearly proud of its rural origins. A few modern details do however contrast with the initial portrait, starting with stylised photos and a glazed wine cellar. In the same vein, the chef orchestrates a modern score founded on tradition. The menu is concise and enticing: beef tartare, 30-day aged on the bone rib of beef, sole meunière, wild seabass...

Name: La Grange
Description: On the banks of the Nive beneath the arcades, this inviting eatery savvily mixes old stones and beams with a contemporary edge. The traditional score, updated with Basque overtones, stars wholesome indulgent flavours: bourguignon-style braised chuck beef and cheeks with a pastry stuffed with fresh herbs and winter veg or the granny-approved house dessert, cocolait. Very popular with the locals, La Grange is just the place to get a glimpse of the real Bayonne.

Name: La Grange des Agapes
Description: Like every true enthusiast, Thierry Barot is a master of multi - tasking. Not content to offer tasty and appetising theme - based menus (vegetables, Provence, asparagus, truffles etc), he regularly runs cookery classes and is the author of a book of chocolate recipes. What a feast!

Name: La Grangée
Description: Chef Jean-Baptiste Girard, an enthusiastic champion of his region, and his Japanese-born wife, Maiko, have turned this village inn around. Local produce (Charolais beef, organic vegetables, saffron…) and what the chef forages take centre stage on the menu - the wild garlic brioche is simply delicious ! Attentive service and tableware crafted by a local artisan make for a delightful experience.

Name: La Grappe d'Or
Description: This flower - decked house built in 1554 could not be more inviting and the characteristic regional interior has lost none of its yesteryear appeal. Classic regional delicacies on the menu: choucroute, baeckeofe, knuckle of ham, stuffed trout, etc.

Name: La Grillade Gourmande
Description: The restaurant specialises in cooking top-drawer produce over a wood fire: whole sea bass with fennel, rib of beef, pluma de pata negra, venison with a peppery sauce poivrade – all dishes are the handiwork of a cheerful chef of Lyon origins. The atmosphere is friendly and buzzy and, come summertime, the garden is bliss.

Name: La Laiterie
Address: 138 avenue de l'Hippodrome, à Lambersart, Lille, 59130, France
Description: Once a dairy, this farmhouse steeped in history lies next to the Parc de la Citadelle and close to the banks of the Deûle Canal. Elegant contemporary rooms inside and a large garden with a terrace are the perfect foil for the chef's creative cuisine, which delves freely into produce from Northern France, with a fondness for surf and turf recipes.

Name: La Lozerette
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: In the heart of the Cévennes, this charming, family-run inn is currently in the hands of the fourth generation. Confidently crafted seasonal dishes that make the most of regional produce set the scene. A few examples: free-range chicken ballotine, poultry jus and roast artichoke or juicy Aubrac steak, potatoes and aubergine caviar, without forgetting the ever-present family specialty: panade de morue (cod and mashed potatoes). Splendid wine list and warm welcome.

Name: La Machine à Coudes
Description: Welcoming and bubbly owner Marlène has a knack for always surrounding herself with a motivated team. They are happy to work with the seasonal produce – scallops and squash – that goes into creating a single set menu at lunchtime, and a more creative and ambitious dinner menu. Good food and wine pairings. An enjoyable moment of bistronomy.

Name: La Maison
Description: In a pedestrian street of downtown Orthez, this vast bistro is housed in what was once a fishing tackle shop. The interior sports a patchwork of mismatched objects. The single set lunch menu changes weekly and at weekends and in the evenings, you will find a concise à la carte lineup with starters to share and upmarket ingredients in a bistro vein.

Name: La Maison
Description: You are made to feel right at home here at La Maison, once a winegrowers' home, with a magnificent stone interior. Creative cuisine is served in the form of dishes in which a number of different elements are juxtaposed. Ludovic Davouze always makes sure to showcase local producers, and enjoys adding an element of surprise, with original combinations of flavours such as just-seared little tuna marinated with chives, with smoked aubergine and miso sauce. The patio is a joy in fine weather.

Name: La Maison Alyette - Domaine de Locguénolé
Address: Route de Port-Louis, Le Hingair, Kervignac, 56700, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A bistro on the Domaine de Locguénolé, La Maison Alyette pays tribute to the château's former owner. Devised by chef Yann Maget (a Meilleur Ouvrier de France), the menu revolves around traditional cuisine made with quality local ingredients. The portions are generous – a case in point being the pork belly and its creamy fregola sarda risotto; the flavours are winning – take the whiting quenelles and their flavoursome bisque; the dishes are moreish – for instance the religieuse with caramel mousse and ice cream. Attractive lunch set menu. View of the gardens, and a lovely terrace.

Name: La Maison Forte
Address: Place de la Maison-Forte, Farnay, 42320, France
Description: The pair at the helm of this imposing stone building – Marie-Jeanne Rault front of house and Loire-native Mickaël Marcoux in the kitchen – are both graduates of MICHELIN-starred establishments. The chef loves to showcase his region, sourcing ingredients predominantly from the Gier Valley. Playing on the full range of textures, he weaves savvy pairings and striking flavours into a consistently indulgent tapestry. The beautifully minimalist Scandinavian-style interior features exposed stonework and simple furnishings. Remember to book in advance – this restaurant is very popular.

Name: La Maison Rouge
Description: Chef Jean Kuentz (dubbed Petit Jean), who learned the ropes in top Parisian establishments, runs this iconic establishment in Colmar's historic centre, a stone's throw from the Petite Venise quarter. In an 11C edifice, he crafts gourmet fare, navigating between regional and more modern dishes, accompanied by well-chosen wines.

Name: La Maison Tourangelle
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Rustic meets modern, a riverside terrace on the banks of the Cher and razor-sharp, ingredient-centric cooking: such are the appeals of this Touraine establishment whose reputation is second to none in the region. In a similar vein, the wine list celebrates local talent.

Name: La Maison d'Estournel
Address: Lieu-dit Leyssac, route de Poumeys, Saint-Estèphe, 33180, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Formerly Château Pomys, Maison d’Estournel oozes understated glamour with its well-heeled interior and fine terrace overlooking the grounds and vineyards. Consultant chef, Jérôme Banctel (Le Gabriel) is behind the new take on classical recipes and seeks to celebrate the gardens and producers of Médoc: green asparagus, smoked Aquitaine sturgeon and Baerii Sturia caviar; roast poultry, morels and supreme sauce. Seasonal and indulgent depicts this restaurant in the heart of wine-growing France.

Name: La Maison d'Œuvres
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
Description: Having earned his stripes in renowned kitchens (Christophe Dufossé, Patrick Henriroux), chef Kévin Dos Santos has set up shop in an old building a stone's throw from the 1 000-year-old church, Église St Pancrace. The decor is understated, with tables upstairs and out on the small courtyard terrace. This 30-something chef crafts his menu to the rhythm of the seasons and the zeitgeist: creamy cauliflower, blood orange and sunflower seed praline; truffle-infused scallop quenelle, celeriac millefeuille, hazelnuts and a reduced jus. The evening menu is updated regularly and calls on more premium ingredients. On weekday lunchtimes, the menu is simpler. The fine wine cellar caters to a wide range of budgets.

Name: La Maison de Petit Pierre
Description: Enthusiastic chef Pierre Augé is at the helm of this restaurant with a personalised decor that is located close to the bullring. He greets each and every customer with an infectious smile because he is there to spread joy with his tasty creative cuisine based on local ingredients! Rather than bask in the media hype, he is clearly driven by a desire to continuously explore new culinary avenues. It's a joy to behold – and tuck into – dishes such as his whisky-marinated pavé de bœuf steak and cauliflower mousseline with vanilla; hake with piperade and green jus; or stracciatella with asparagus and bacon tuile. A buzzy, friendly vibe, enhanced by the personality of the chef, and the warm, cheerful service of his wife, adds the final flourish: recommended!

Name: La Maison des Blés - Le Bouche à Oreille
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: A contemporary setting, a modern interior and a choice of two venues to treat yourself to a slap-up meal: Brasserie Louis and its traditional lineup or its gourmet sibling, Le Bouche à Oreille. Slick, professional service and food that showcases top-notch ingredients (including lobster, scallops and foie gras) with a creative twist. Modern, comfortable guestrooms.

Name: La Maison des Bois
Description: Beneath a thatched roof and smothered in Virginia creeper, this spruce, hundred-year-old inn has been welcoming travellers since 1926. Three generations have preserved its authentic character, whilst breathing a new lease of life thanks to a tasteful restoration. The same spirit prevails on the menu, with traditional fare and market-fresh dishes made with premium produce. The house signature is lobster stew in season. Terrace in the shade of old plane trees. The epitome of a French country inn!

Name: La Maison des Toqués
Address: 26 rue de la Prée-aux-Ducs, Noirmoutier-en-l'Île, 85330, France
Description: Aurore and Sébastien Duchenne share the same passion for top-quality regional produce, often organic, which they transform into delicious recipes that capture the zeitgeist and are inspired by market availability. As you enter, you are greeted by a colourful, modern interior whose blue and white walls are adorned with artwork, providing the perfect foil to elegantly plated ingredients such as lobster, local oysters, John Dory or royal Charmilles pigeon. Booking highly advisable.

Name: La Mangeoire
Description: Near Lake Madine, this beautifully restored farmstead sports a chic rustic vibe, depicted by the straw-filled manger (its namesake) that continues to line one wall. It is the HQ of Quentin Pierre, a nature lover who spares no effort in bringing local producers into the mix thanks to ingredients such as trout from Saint-Mihiel, pork from Vilotte-sur-Aire, organic veg from Belleray. His cuisine is seasonal, fresh and simple. The tasting menu incorporates more premium ingredients (foie gras, arctic char sweetbreads). The wine list shines the spotlight on local Côtes de Meuse vintages.

Name: La Mangeoire
Address: 2 rue du Castrum (Le Bourg), Floirac, 46600, France
Description: In this picturesque Lot village, the traveller cannot fail but notice the handsome limestone edifice with a slate roof, flanked by a terrace and Belle Époque conservatory. The globe-trotting chef demonstrates a weakness for exotic combinations: velvety, humus-like aubergines, burnt rye bread, fried Camus artichoke and pork fillet dried in the hearthplace; lightly seared secreto pata negro pork with peanuts and ginger, roast fennel and whole wheat noodles. Bistronomic in style, internationally sourced and strewn with tributes to Asia and North African spices.

Name: La Marmite du Pêcheur
Address: Boulevard des Tilleuls, Les Mées, 04190, France
Description: This restaurant, a former mill, stands at the foot of the village’s iconic jagged cliffs, Les Pénitents. It serves fish and seafood specialities (bouillabaisse to order), together with succulent meats, including lamb from Sisteron. The interior sports a modern vibe, offset by an old mill wheel that endows the interior with a characterful dimension.

Name: La Maréa
Description: Opposite the sea and the ochre-coloured rocks of the Estérel mountains and looking down on the beach and port of La Figueirette, this restaurant was founded in the 1950s by a local fisherman. It has passed into the capable hands of Jérôme Cervera, a former fishmonger. The chef whips up a menu featuring ultra-fresh seafood and carefully crafted dishes, such as lightly seared red mullet served with fruity olive oil and seasonal vegetables. The attentive and bright service adds to your enjoyment of the meal. At lunch and dinner, an appealing set menu reprises dishes from the à la carte menu – tuck in on the terrace or in the pretty dining area with a sea view.

Name: La Matelote
Description: A family-run business that pays tribute to women must be a good sign! A “matelote” is the fisherman’s wife, whose talent cannot be equalled when it comes to preparing fish, just like that of this establishment devoted body and soul to seafood (but not to the exclusion of other ingredients). Fish and shellfish are crafted in keeping with culinary tradition and with the firm intention of encouraging sustainable fishing. Save room for the patriotic line-up of Gallic desserts, such as soufflé, the house signature dish.

Name: La Mercerie
Description: Just a hop from Marseille’s historic Canebière, this bolthole is one of the stars of the city’s fine dining scene. At the helm is English-born chef, Harry Cummins, assisted by Quebec-born sommelière, Laura Vidal. A sensibly priced menu sets the lunchtime scene, while a more creative five-course cast takes front stage in the evening. A feelgood bistronomic score and seasonal produce: finely diced veggies, a barbecue edge and savvy seasonings. A cosmopolitan team and a funky R&B soundtrack depict this eatery that is almost always fully booked, although you will have more chance of finding a seat at non-peak times, at the counter facing the kitchen or, from April to October, on the terrace on Cours Saint Louis.

Name: La Mirande
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Behind the Palais des Papes, this townhouse has been knocking around for over seven centuries. Michele Donvito, Alexandre Mazzia’s ex executive chef, rolls out a several-course set menu. Each step of the instinctive, creative score features three ingredients, one main dish and two sides. His plant-based, Provençal-leaning, healthy approach is enhanced with citrus and other fruits, spices and garden herbs in addition to a distinct fondness for surf-turf pairings: carrots, herring and tobiko eggs, or courgette flowers stuffed with pecorino cheese and creamy plankton. Whether it is in the sublime 18C interior or in the exquisite garden, you can expect a heroically wondrous gourmet experience.

Name: La Musardière
Description: Located in the heart of the village, close to Claude Monet's house and the Musée des Impressionnismes Giverny, La Musardière serves a bistronomy lunch menu at Le M and more ambitious dining options in the evening at Révélations. The convivial, contemporary bistro setting is complemented by a pleasant terrace that receives plenty of sun in summer. A number of guestrooms are available, should you wish to extend your stay.

Name: La Mère Germaine
FacilitiesAndServices: Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Jean Cocteau used to eat at this local institution, which has been serving fresh fish and seafood since 1938. It is lovely just to sit on the terrace and gaze out over the harbour!

Name: La Mère Germaine
Description: En route to the French Riviera, Paris's upper crust, including movie stars from Mistinguett to Jean Gabin and Fernandel, used to stop off in this village so beloved of wine buffs. The restaurant, still named after its 1922 founder, Germaine Vion, features huge murals evoking Belle Époque Paris, in the style of Toulouse-Lautrec, and a delightful terrace commanding a panoramic view. The Mediterranean-inspired cuisine elevates the ingredients and vegetables of Provence. The splendid wine list includes a good selection of Châteauneuf-du-Pape labels.

Name: La Mère Hamard
Description: This stone-built inn, which opened in 1903, is a genuine institution. The delightful dining room is flanked by a welcoming terrace shaded by wisteria, ideal to sample delicate, generous dishes, tinged with the occasional exotic influence. Attentive welcome and a few guestrooms for overnight stays.

Name: La Méditerranée
Description: This elegantly understated establishment opposite the Odéon Theatre pays tribute to the sea and the flavour of authentic produce. In a bright space decorated with Mediterranean frescoes, guests tuck into egg mayonnaise with king crab and lime, fragrant bouillabaisse or delicately golden sole meunière. Attentive hospitality and highly professional service are the icing on the cake.

Name: La Palantxa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: This delightful green half-timbered Basque house nestling in the hills is only a few minutes outside Bayonne. The property can be traced back to as early as 1602 when it was a tavern. Inside, stone and wood meet contemporary furnishings in an uncluttered setting. Chef Antoine Chuard rolls out several set menus that showcase creative recipes crafted with cherry-picked ingredients.

Name: La Pap Restaurant
Description: The Papin couple have set up their contemporary restaurant in a tastefully restored old building marrying rustic and chic elements. An open kitchen, exposed beams and raw materials make for an inviting space, in which the chef – the son of a farmer and a keen traveller – showcases modern cuisine inspired by his experiences in London, Montreal and Tokyo. Local produce, seafood influences and creative touches are perfectly expressed in beautifully presented dishes, such as fish terrine with smoked eel, crab and lemon sauce.

Name: La Part des Anges
Description: Tucked away in a pedestrian street behind the marina, this bistro was opened by two friends who are familiar faces around the Gulf of Saint Tropez and connoisseurs of its top restaurants. The chef honed his skills at Fréchon, after a stint in Grimaud; front of house, cordial and meticulous service comes courtesy of a pro from the local scene. The capacity of the cosy little space has been significantly increased by the addition of a terrace; music from the 1970s-90s, especially chanson française, makes up the soundtrack. Expect generous and discerning bistronomy cuisine. The dishes change with the seasons, and, with vegetarian and gluten-free options, there is something for everyone.

Name: La Part des Anges
Description: The market-fresh menu demonstrates deep respect for the seasons and a desire to highlight the work of local producers. Healthy appetites are encouraged and appreciated and the front-of-house team is pleasantly attentive. Its enduring popularity with the locals says it all!

Name: La Passerelle
Description: The chef now at the helm of this maritime-inspired restaurant, where she once trained with her father, is giving us her own modern take on family tradition. She likes to add good concentrated jus to her dishes (octopus with pork jus) as well as sweet-and-sour flavours (langoustine, turnip, almonds). She is also a sommelier, and puts her heart and soul into coming up with optimal food and wine pairings.

Name: La Passerelle
Description: At La Passerelle, on the banks of the Seine, chef Mickaël Meziane invites you into a bright dining space with a large counter, a green wall and a pleasant terrace overlooking the river. Celery royale, rockfish soup and pavlova with exotic fruits are part of a spot-on skilful culinary offering that is served with care by an attentive team. Ingredient quality and technical precision take precedence at this place run with sincerity.

Name: La Petite Maison
Description: You come to this lovely restaurant ensconced in a terracotta-coloured "little house" on the outskirts of Cogolin. It is run by Damien Levivien, a trained pastry chef who learned the ropes under Jean Sulpice and Yannick Alléno. He and his wife serve precise and elegant market cuisine that won't break the bank. House-made pâté en croûte, ravioli crafted on site, meticulous dishes and classic desserts are all skilfully made. In this intimate setting, the terrace shaded by wisteria and mulberry trees adds to the charm, offering a peaceful stopover on the outskirts of Saint-Tropez.

Name: La Petite Plage
Description: In this restaurant in the village port, Eric Frechon devises the menu, and the sea does the rest. Enjoy a new take on flavoursome Mediterranean cuisine, as you bury your feet in the sand overlooking the yachts, ever a subject of conversation. On summer evenings, a DJ provides the soundtrack, as is the norm in Saint-Tropez! Attentive service despite the bustle.

Name: La Petite Table
Address: 7 quai de la Pêcherie, Capbreton, 40130, France
Description: Whether seated on the terrace or inside, you are promised an enticing culinary interlude at this really inviting compact restaurant on Capbreton harbour. Generous and colourful dishes enhanced by citrus fruit and spices get to the heart of the matter, showcasing the local catch, lamb from the Pyrenees and vegetables from a market gardener in nearby Tosse. Don't miss the chocolate tart – a proper showstopper!

Name: La Petite École
Description: This restaurant moved into the premises of the former village school a few years ago. The delicate, flavoursome cuisine is definitely worth an A. Ten out of ten, too, for the chef, a lover of fine produce, who concocts precise, succulent recipes. Even better, it is excellent value for money - if only our school canteen had been like this!

Name: La Pie qui Couette
Description: Bang in the heart of Nîmes’ bustling food market, this eatery, run by a seasoned chef, will knock the socks off your tastebuds. Market fare crafted with fresher than fresh produce from the neighbouring market stalls. House specialties include matured meat, cod brandade, chopped beef tartare and île flottante (vanilla custard and meringue). Hearty helpings, an intelligent wine list, tightly packed tables and a good-natured, jovial vibe. No bookings possible, open from 11.30am to 3pm and always packed (try and come off peak at the weekend).

Name: La Pierrevue
Address: 2 place de la Mairie, Saint-Rogatien, 17220, France
Description: "There are six seasons in the year": with this saying in mind, chef Cécile Richard adapts her recipes to the times, with a drive for creativity that can be sensed in her fresh and precise cuisine. Locally caught fish, fruit and vegetables from organic market gardeners, aromatic herbs and flowers from the garden can be enjoyed in this farmhouse, converted in a pleasant rustic style. Attractive glass-paned wine cellar. New menu every two months.

Name: La Pinède
Address: Chemin du Langoustier, Ile de Porquerolles, 83400, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Patrons of this out-of-the-way hotel are collected from the village in a shuttle bus; the laidback restaurant of Le Mas du Langoustier is only open at lunchtime. The menu showcases the Mediterranean and Provençal dishes: pistou soup, "panier du pêcheur façon bourride", grilled fish and crayfish etc – to savour against a backdrop of Mediterranean plants and the sea: simply sit back, tuck in and enjoy the moment.

Name: La Pinède
Address: Strada di Cala Rossa, Lecci, 20137, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Whether for a relaxed lunch by the beach or dinner beneath the arbour, the intimate and romantic setting is utterly magnificent. The simple and delicious Mediterranean cuisine is a celebration of local ingredients. Herbs and vegetables from the 3 000m2 organic kitchen garden are often incorporated. And let's not forget the maturing cellar for cheeses and the enticing wine list.

Name: La Place de Mougins
Description: This delightful eatery, bang on the village square as the name suggests, is depicted by a chic yet cosy vibe and a bubbly culinary score courtesy of a creative and enthusiastic chef. Every month, he showcases a seasonal ingredient from truffles to asparagus, etc. We recommend asking for a seat in the conservatory.

Name: La Plage
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Wheelchair access
Description: This beachfront restaurant has looked out onto the ebbing and flowing tides since 1924. An idyllic setting in which to enjoy dishes that showcase fine ingredients, in particular fish and seafood, such as line-caught pollock, shallots, potatoes, mushrooms in a seafood emulsion…

Name: La Plage Casadelmar
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace
Description: On the Benedettu peninsula, tucked away in the vegetation by the beach, this contemporary haven is the younger sibling of Casadelmar – its "casual" beachfront version. Everything happens on the terrace looking out to the Gulf of Porto Vecchio from beneath driftwood pergolas that blend into the landscape. In this divine setting, select your dishes from a menu of refined brasserie cuisine with Italian influences: vitello tonnato, tuna crudo, fritto misto, grilled lobster, appetising pasta dishes and fresh salads. The classic desserts absolutely do the job: profiteroles, tiramisu, lemon meringue pie. The freshness and quality of the ingredients inspire confidence.

Name: La Plancha
Description: The polished culinary score of this modest establishment makes it well worth hunting out. The stripped-back, competent and a tad creative dishes are packed in striking flavours: e.g. flame-licked slices of monkfish with a wasabi foam or roast pollock with green peas, verbena and apricot. The textbook perfect profiteroles are wickedly addictive.

Name: La Pointe du Cap Coz
Address: 153 avenue de la Pointe, au Cap Coz, Fouesnant, 29170, France
Description: This white cottage seems to sit right on the ocean. The chef has chosen this isolated location to craft delicious cuisine in line with his commitment to local surf and turf produce. The result is beautifully presented dishes, such as slow-cooked pork cheeks in cider vinegar served with cabbage and apples baked in salted butter.

Name: La Ponche
Description: This iconic Saint-Tropez establishment stands looking out to sea in the neighbourhood of La Ponche. The Mediterranean cuisine showcases the catch of the day and locally sourced vegetables, as well as high-quality meats. While the lunchtime menu keeps things simple, in the evening guests can indulge in dishes such as fresh prawn ravioli with spicy Calabrian sausage, prawn head bisque with almonds, or the day's catch grilled and served with sorrel cream and sauce provençale. An extensive cocktail list rounds off the experience perfectly.

Name: La Poste et Hôtel La Reconce
Description: The Restaurant de la Poste is run by a chef who hails from the village, ably assisted by his wife. His ambition is clear: to regale diners with modern dishes that celebrate good local produce – braised Charolais beef shank wrapped in celeriac, with pot-au-feu bouillon and wasabi, is a good example. Well-kept rooms, should you wish to stay over.

Name: La Poule au Pot
Description: The great classics of the French culinary repertoire are given an overhaul here by Jean-François Piège. Service on a silver tray, old-fashioned bistro decor, zinc counter: it has all the trappings. It's Audiard's Paris down to a T... right down to the food: onion gratinée, quenelle of arctic char, beef chuck hash, Colbert fried whiting with tartar sauce.

Name: La Poya
Description: In a mountain-inspired decor, the chef serves up good-quality traditional cuisine that often takes meat as its starting point… but does not exclude the odd Asian note (eg gravelax salmon tataki marinated in beetroot, served with mustard sorbet). The dishes are beautifully presented and service comes with a smile. A good place to recharge your batteries after hitting the slopes on your skis!

Name: La Presqu'île
Address: 1105 avenue Notre-Dame - esplanade Port-Miou, Cassis, 13260, France
Description: At the tip of the calanque of Port-Miou, this drop-dead seaside property commands a breathtaking vista over Cap Canaille from the conservatory dining room and the terrace. The chef rolls out polished, modern Mediterranean fare, crafted mainly from regional goodies (red mullet, mackerel, squid from the Mediterranean, veg and local goat’s cheese), but also from further afar (like pluma iberico).

Name: La Quincaillerie
Description: In a sleepy village poised between Cognac and Bordeaux, this former hardware store boasts an imposing wooden staircase and a wrought-iron first-floor gallery, together with a buzzy vibe and a homespun retro look. The score errs towards patriotic French, dotted with a handful of international accents and is escorted by a savvily curated wine cellar (and shop) that can be seen on the ground-floor. The lunchtime weekday set menu is a steal.

Name: La Quintessence
Description: Housed in a converted 16C Jesuit refectory, this restaurant in the Presqu'île district has plenty of character, with its stone walls, columns and arches, its vaulted ceiling, hardwood floors and tall windows. Chef Anthony Baud cooks up balanced modern cuisine that emphasises the freshness and quality of the ingredients, in dishes such as Arctic char with pak choi, or a delicious persimmon dessert incorporating ginger and pumpkin seed praline. The set menus are changed up on a regular basis to showcase the ingredients of the season.

Name: La R'mize
Address: 160 rue du Vieux-Village, Les Gets, 74260, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
Description: In the village, near the church, this family-run restaurant serves tasty traditional cuisine. An experienced chef delights with well-crafted recipes: creamy burrata, tomatoes, peaches, peas and crunchy almonds; Arborio risotto with Abondance cheese, scallop carpaccio and shellfish jus. The menu also includes classic Savoyard specialities, like an indulgent gratin or Savoyard fondue with champagne!

Name: La Racine et la Moelle
Description: In a lane of the historic town, this neo-bistro is depicted by a bubbly vibe and spot-on cooking in the zeitgeist. Chef Julie changes the menu constantly, rolling out modern indulgent recipes like grilled squid, melt-in-the-mouth Aubrac hanger steak and a small red fruit almond financier cake to finish. By her side, Michael’s carefully curated cellar unveils a natural wine focus. This bouncy, vibrant venue has captured the hearts of Figeac.

Name: La Rascasse
Address: Le Provençal, 113 place Saint-Pierre, Giens, 83400, France
Description: At the tip of the Giens peninsula, this hotel-restaurant, which sports a colourful, restored façade commands a knockout view of the sea and the Îles d’Or. In a warm, timeless setting, Sébastien Graize signs spot-on Mediterranean fare that pays tribute to local market gardeners from Vars and fishermen from Niel. The house signature is bouillabaisse, packed in flavour and aromas. The fashionably refurbished guestrooms are blissful, as is the saltwater pool carved out of the rock down by the shore.

Name: La Rissole
Description: The name of this bistro pays tribute to a famous chef and culinary writer of the last century, while celebrating the joy of authentic flavours. The concise menu highlights the seasons and regional produce (snails, Touraine pork and freshwater fish). Those with little time to spare at lunchtime will be delighted to know they offer a three-course menu served all at once on a tray, alongside a pedigree à la carte lineup. Bookings recommended.

Name: La Roche Le Roy
Description: This pretty little manor house on the outskirts of town has recently been refurbished and modernised, all the way from the decoration to the kitchens, the domain of chef Maximilien Bridier. Taking an enthusiastic approach to high-quality ingredients, he presents elegant, precise dishes with no frills. Without fail, the menu features a vegetarian option. There is a fine selection of wines by the glass, and the service is attentive. Sit out on the terrace on warm days.

Name: La Rotonde
Address: Hôtel du Palais, 1 avenue de l'Impératrice, Biarritz, 64200, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Perhaps the most iconic hotel on the Atlantic coast, the prestigious Hôtel du Palais needs no introduction. In elegant, historical surroundings overlooking the ocean, its traditional cuisine (such as the "Crêpe Suzy", a tribute to Raymond Oliver) sometimes cedes its place in the spotlight to more contemporary creations. Fish and seafood and the best of the Aquitaine terroir are never far away, a case in point being the abalone delicately confit in seaweed butter, the glazed John Dory with fishbone jus and its "marine garden", or the "rhub'algue" dessert, which brilliantly combines the subtle acidity of rhubarb with the brininess of seaweed. Precise and efficient service.

Name: La Rotonde
Address: Le Negresco, 37 promenade des Anglais, Nice, 06000, France
Description: The rotunda-shaped brasserie of the legendary luxury hotel has resolutely entered the modern world. In this light-filled space (with a terrace), you choose from a menu (designed by Michelin-starred chef Virginie Basselot) that celebrates a flavoursome and colourful cuisine full of Mediterranean flair, with nods to Nice's traditions.

Name: La Route d'Argent
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: On the ground floor of the hotel, this restaurant, which sports a bright, modern interior, is enthusiastically helmed by Loïc and Océane Gay. Regional produce (Aubrac beef and trout) takes front stage in soul-warming, indulgent dishes: persillade of lamb sweetbreads or squab breast. Traditional aligot (mashed potatoes and cheese) is served with the main course.

Name: La Récréation
Address: 70 rue de la Vialotte, Le Bourg, Les Arques, 46250, France
Description: School’s out! In its place, this gently nostalgic establishment has a classroom - style dining room, courtyard terrace and kitchen garden in the old playground. Contemporary cuisine.

Name: La Récréation Gourmande
Description: In this former schoolhouse, an old stove presides, with a dunce's hat perched on top! Whatever the standard of the class, everyone can tuck into the generous and tasty cooking, which makes the ingredients the star of the class. A Récréation Gourmande indeed!

Name: La Régalade Saint-Honoré
Description: Bruno Doucet regales foodies in the Halles neighbourhood with dishes that sing an ode to fresh market and country produce. After titillating your tastebuds with the chef's delicious terrine, dig into pan-fried snails, mushrooms and chorizo, followed by braised chuck steak with a bourguignon garnish or the “famous” rice pudding with a dairy caramel. Fine wine list.

Name: La Réserve
Description: In a 16C former larder and storeroom, nowadays the Citadelle Hotel, the culinary score reveals a gourmet streak paired with a generous nature: roast turbotin, butternut in almond milk and baby veg; fillet of organic Moselle beef, potato pie and Chinese cabbage… A storeroom with plenty of surprises in store!

Name: La Réserve de Nice
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Elegant, Art Deco cruise liner - inspired decor. Enjoy refined cuisine and superb views of the Bay of Angels and the Estérel mountains.

Name: La Réserve à la Plage
Description: The Pampelonne beach version of the luxurious Réserve Ramatuelle casts an exclusive seaside spell by way of a large wooden cabana with cane light fixtures, mismatched furniture and a chic bohemian vibe signed Philippe Starck. Chef Nicolas Cantrel bewitches with his Riviera-inspired cuisine, starring carefully sourced meat and the local catch of the day, among others. Open from 10.30am to 6.30pm (lunch at midday and 3pm). Suitably stylish service.

Name: La Salamandre
Description: In a picture postcard medieval village overlooking the River Cher, this eatery, located in an outhouse of the castle of Saint-Aignan, sports a trendy bistro vibe beneath an attractive timber ceiling. The chef rolls out a fresh, colourful lineup, including a vegetarian menu. Terrace at the foot of the chateau.

Name: La Saulire
Address: 16 place du Rocher, Courchevel 1850, Courchevel, 73120, France
Description: An interior decked out in pale wood and decorated with old mountain objects is the authentic and inviting setting in which chef Benoît Redondo cooks up meticulous food and makes no bones about serving the famous Savoyard fondue alongside Périgord truffles. The welcome and service are extremely attentive. N.B. The restaurant is closed at lunchtime in good weather, to let skiers enjoy the snow on the resort's slopes.

Name: La Serre
Description: An explosion of greenery sets the scene for a splendid lineup of dishes, scattered with the odd creative touch. The spot-on result stars punchy flavours and meticulous plating. Meals are served in a magnificent greenhouse or on the alfresco patio that is bliss in fine weather.

Name: La Sittelle
Description: This attractive 1940’s villa is enjoying a new lease of life thanks to two partners, formerly of Locguénolé chateau. The chef uses regional produce in recipes with a creative spin and a fondness for surf and turf dishes. Keen to work exclusively with locally sourced ingredients, he has banned exotic fruits, chocolate and vanilla and uses chicory instead of coffee. Warm seamless service.

Name: La Source de Veules-les-Roses
Description: This charming village dotted with windmills, watercress beds and gardens was a popular holiday destination for Parisian writers, painters and intellectuals in the 19C. In a bright, cosy bistro, the chef serves up indulgent modern cuisine featuring quality ingredients – Arctic char, free-range chicken, vegetables from local market gardeners, oysters from Normandy… with inventive little flourishes on every plate.

Name: La Source des Sens
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: The setting is strikingly contemporary, with black walls and carpeting and atmospheric lighting. The food is equally up-to-date, thanks to the commitment of chef Pierre Weller, who slips in the odd tribute to Japan’s culinary culture, while excelling in the art of precise plating. The Source also proposes guestrooms for overnight stays, together with a luxurious spa to pamper your senses.

Name: La Suite
Description: Slightly out of the historic centre, you will sample seasonal family favourites tailored to today’s palates and entirely made from scratch. The chef is single-minded in his goal for flavour before all else, demonstrated by a yellow onion and camembert pie. A concise menu, seasonal produce, generous helpings and straightforward flavours. All of which in a smart, buzzy vibe in the company of numerous locals.

Name: La Suite S'il Vous Plaît
Address: 20 boulevard Franklin-Roosevelt, Les Sables d’Olonne, 85100, France
Description: Located behind the casino and the beaches, this establishment is a breath of fresh air on the local restaurant scene. In a trendy bistro decor, chef Mélanie Sire painstakingly calibrates a lineup that changes every three weeks or so. Her skilful play on textures and flavours includes creations such as a new take on vitello-style pork, flame-seared baby squid and a delicious blackberry-themed dessert. Can we have some more... s'il vous plait?

Name: La Sérafine
Description: This chef, originally from Vietnam, meticulously prepares inventive and instinctive cuisine that is constantly evolving. The single multi-course set menu allies local produce and exotic touches in dishes that are colourful and fragrant. With its exposed beams and hardwood floors, the traditional interior opens onto a veranda that leads onto a pleasant terrace overlooking an imposing metal statue of a rearing horse.

Name: La Table
Address: Domaine Misincu, lieu-dit Misincu, Cagnano, 20228, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
Description: Established in an airy hotel nestled betwixt land and sea, La Table elegantly embodies Reine Sammut’s Mediterranean score. Indulgent and authentic, her approach highlights local produce (Abatucci veal, Centuri fish) and fresh produce from the property’s kitchen garden. Each dish is a masterpiece of drool-worthy flavours and plating, exemplified by baby courgettes with flowers stuffed with brocciu or loin of Mediterranean seabass confit in olive oil. A quintessentially romantic setting with a view of the sea from the panoramic terrace. Slick, seamless service adds the final flourish.

Name: La Table - Hôtel Clarance
Address: 32 rue de la Barre, Lille, 59000, France
Description: In the heart of historical Lille, an 18C mansion houses this elegant restaurant in its salons decked out with period wood panelling and in what was once the library. The decor sees heritage features skilfully blended with contemporary design details. In the set menus, which change with the seasons, regional and seasonal produce are given pride of place – scallops, red seabream, saddle of lamb and autumn mushrooms. Peaceful terrace for summer days.

Name: La Table - Maison Lobies
Description: In the middle of the village, with the church on one side and fields on the other, this beautiful 18C manor house with a courtyard to the front has a refined, classical decor. The premises are both home and place of work for an enthusiastic, smiling couple with experience in some of the world's top restaurants. Sun Young, a pastry chef who hails from South Korea, and chef Jérémie work together to devise an appealing, delicious and rather traditional menu: super-soft poultry with crispy skin and an excellent, generous fricassee of chanterelle mushrooms, and a buttery potato purée; beef chuck confit in its jelly sprinkled with hazelnut and boosted by a real mustard and shallot sauce! As for the desserts (floating island, Tahitian vanilla crème anglaise or raspberry cheesecake), it's as simple as this: they're all mouth-wateringly good.

Name: La Table - Sébastien Gravé
Description: Sébastien Gravé, something of a celebrity on the Bayonne bistronomic scene, is back on his home turf. He cheerfully crafts dishes inspired by the best produce South-West France has to offer, including hake from Saint-Jean-de-Luz au naturel, Basque trout and Noir de Bigorre pork bacon. You can eat at the zinc-topped counter, at the large table d'hôtes with friends or in the kitchen, where there is a table for two for a more immersive experience. A buzzy, bouncy vibe sets the scene in this feel-good establishment.

Name: La Table 101
Description: In the Part-Dieu neighbourhood, not far from Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse, Olivier and Maryline Delbergues's restaurant delivers market-fresh cuisine with the odd creative twist: guinea fowl supreme with crayfish, red cabbage braised in red wine and roasted salsify; pollack with seaweed polenta and grilled sobrasada.

Name: La Table Floralie
Description: This is the town-centre spot that everyone in Aix is talking about! The first venture of this young couple, the restaurant is an appealing modern space with an open kitchen. The chef conjures up neat contemporary dishes that are full of flavour, highlighting primarily local seasonal produce. He enjoys interacting with guests, especially when it comes to recommending the Savoie wines about which he is so passionate. A family atmosphere prevails here.

Name: La Table Saint Thomas
Description: In the quiet setting of a residential neighbourhood, this restaurant – housed in a converted carpentry workshop – is run by a couple of industry professionals. As for the food, the chef combines tradition with the four seasons to rustle up tasteful, simple and honest cuisine: Label Rouge salmon gravlax, Sichuan pepper emulsion, beetroot gel; turbot, asparagus gratin and Champagne sauce; rum baba with pineapple brunoise.

Name: La Table by La Villa
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: La Table is part of La Villa, whose luxurious decor fades in front of the jaw-dropping view of the bay, citadel and mountains. The focus is on premium regional produce which is married with Italian-inspired recipes: Milanese veal cutlet, carpaccio of marinated Corsican veal “al Limone”, a new take on parmigiana, etc. Everything is served alfresco on the incredible panoramic terrace. Simpler (but equally delicious) lunch menu.

Name: La Table d'Aimé
Description: Established within a winery and appointed in a style that blends Provençal and industrial elements (wrought iron, barrels of wine, bare brick walls), the restaurant offers inspired market-fresh food, organic whenever possible, washed down with wines from the estate. In summertime, the leafy patio is irresistible.

Name: La Table d'Alaïs
Description: Within the medieval walled city, this is your best bet if you want to avoid the tourist traps. Up the stairs, you'll find the pared-back dining area leading onto a courtyard terrace for dining in fine weather. On the menu, traditional and modern go hand in hand: 64-degree egg, truffle and button mushrooms; cassoulet with Castelnaudary beans and duck confit; pavlova with seasonal fruit and vanilla mascarpone cream.

Name: La Table d'Alva
Address: 19 place du Général-de-Gaulle, Le Vaudreuil, 27100, France
Description: A stone's throw from the River Eure, this modern restaurant showcases the talents of chef Valentin Harou and pastry chef Alice Picard, both of whom trained at prestigious establishments such as Le Meurice, Le K2 and L'Oiseau Blanc. Their cuisine aligns with the seasons and makes the most of local produce, particularly by drawing ingredients from the chef's father's vegetable garden and a permaculture farm. This meticulous sourcing pays tribute to Normandy's terroir through creative dishes incorporating nods to the producers.

Name: La Table d'Angèle
Description: This restaurant flanked by a conservatory proposes appetising bistro food in a contemporary setting. Dishes you may find on the menu include roasted calf sweetbreads, pan-fried chanterelles and lardons, meurette sauce; Angus entrecôte and fresh chips from Savoie... Quiet terrace to the rear.

Name: La Table d'Auzeville
Description: In this white house in the heart of a village in the suburbs of Toulouse, the chef serves up generous traditional cuisine, including dishes such as fillet of duck with a spicy reduction or tournedos of beef with morel mushrooms. For dessert, a crunchy strawberry tartlet with home-made pistachio ice cream. In fine weather, enjoy your meal on the shady terrace.

Name: La Table d'Edgar
Description: Chef Sébastien David signs an enticing score using top-notch, mainly local Brittany ingredients. Expertly balanced flavours, consummate cooking and a sprinkling of bold combinations define the score: pollock paired with papaya-samphire-marjoram seasoning or a fennel-themed dessert flanked by a white chocolate ganache and bergamot seasoning. This painstaking attention to detail is also mirrored in the bright, relaxed interior whose pleasant lounge-dining area is set in a conservatory, adding both warmth and light to this town centre establishment.

Name: La Table d'Elka
Description: Chef Laurent Kleczewski and his wife Élodie have set up shop in a renovated farmhouse with a contemporary extension here in Varengeville-sur-Mer. An orchard and a small herb garden that they tend themselves surround the property and are visible through the large picture windows. The chef showcases the cornucopia of Normandy, such as locally fished turbot and seabass, to craft indulgent fare packed in flavour. Solidly anchored in purebred Gallic technique, this fine dining score is enhanced by the odd exotic note: fish of the day with a dashi-spiked butter and local seaweed or fillet of beef in a pepper sauce with olives and raisins.

Name: La Table d'Emilie
Description: The house where the poet Achille Maffre de Baugé was born is home to this very popular restaurant: the delicious and meticulous cuisine is anchored in French tradition (the pâté en croûte is excellent!). Made using fresh produce, this is particularly artfully plated food. To be enjoyed in a dining space with a vaulted ceiling or out on the pleasant patio.

Name: La Table d'Émilie
Description: At the helm of this friendly restaurant, Émilie and Yoann showcase first-rate produce in the form of a market-fresh set menu that offers excellent value for money at lunchtime and sets its sights higher in the evening. The chef has a sure touch, especially when it comes to desserts. In fine weather, head for the pleasant garden terrace.

Name: La Table d'Éole
Description: Sylvain Gauthey (formerly of La Maison des Cariatides in Dijon) and Valentine have set up shop in a beautiful traditional stone house in the heart of this Burgundy wine-growing village. Instead of a set menu, there is a short à la carte menu of dishes the names of which alone are mouthwatering. The chef's expertise shines through in every course with consistently winning flavour combinations (scallops, cauliflower mousseline, green apple and hazelnut sauce vierge, hint of ginger). The sweet finale hits a perfectly seasonal note with a dessert starring pear. The dining area comprises two distinct spaces: the first is contemporary, with grey tones and a glass-walled kitchen; the second, warmer and more traditional, is laid out beneath a stone vaulted ceiling.

Name: La Table de Balthazar
Description: You can expect a meal in a smart, stylish brasserie vein, crafted by talented Benjamin Jourdren. The score of this restaurant, set in what must be Rennes’ most elegant hotel, shines the spotlight on first-class, primarily local Breton produce. The lunchtime menu is simple and becomes more ambitious in the evenings as the chef adds a novel, inspired spin to traditional recipes and ingredients, illustrated by roast croaker with a gutsy fishbone, fennel and cherry jus, or cuttlefish with spider crab and samphire. Fine tableware adorns the elegantly laid tables, while the eye is often drawn to the lovely outdoor patio, visible through the conservatory windows.

Name: La Table de Beaurecueil
Description: This restaurant is housed in a former sheep barn and features a resolutely contemporary design (only a few of the original rustic features remain). It offers “cuisine du terroir” based on high quality produce. Wine by the glass.

Name: La Table de Biar
Description: Just a few kilometres from Montpellier yet deep in the countryside, this 18C Montpellier retreat is set within a 45ha estate, planted with bamboo groves and home to grazing horses. An old wine storehouse is home to the restaurant, which has a slightly industrial aesthetic. The open kitchen turns out lovely seasonal dishes featuring vegetables, Mediterranean fish and meat from local purebreds – think mussels marinated in fennel or grilled octopus. Surprise lunch set menu and à la carte options.

Name: La Table de Catusseau
Description: At the helm are Kendji Wongsodikromo, originally from New Caledonia, and his wife Nadège, who attentively manages the restaurant floor. In an unadorned building of the characteristic sandy hue of local stone with large bay windows, the chef cooks up colourful modern cuisine inspired by the market. Both local and international influences can be detected: coconut-ginger-verbena ceviche of dolfinfish, tomato-Espelette pepper sorbet, young rabbit terrine with garden herbs.

Name: La Table de Charrou
Address: Mas de Charrou, 300 route de Charrou, Limogne-en-Quercy, 46260, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the upper reaches of this village on the Causse de Limogne, this unusual restaurant is housed in an old stone farmhouse. It has been set up by a couple, sommeliers by trade and returnees from a stint in New Zealand, who learned the art of cutting meat from the village butcher, who happens to be the proprietress's father. As a result, they serve only local meats (from the Lot, Aveyron and Tarn-et-Garonne), prepared nose to tail, then matured, smoked, simmered, grilled or made into a terrine – accompanied by crispy, succulent chips cooked in beef fat. Don't miss the wood-fired leg of lamb, cooked in the farmhouse's old bread oven on Sundays. Some 200 labels, including organic and biodynamic wines, make up a list that the lady of the house knows like the back of her hand.

Name: La Table de Clément Paillard
Description: This contemporary restaurant is housed in a modern building opposite Cathédrale St Maurice, with large picture windows affording views onto the historical edifice. The bright, intimate space complete with open kitchen has blue-grey carpeting and light wood tables. Clément Paillard, formerly at Aux Jeunes Pousses, is at the helm, dedicated to creative, seasonal cooking made with local produce. Plays on textures are a feature in dishes such as veal sweetbreads and artichokes, wasabi peas, and sole with asparagus purée, tempura and brunoise. In the evening, there is a more ambitious tasting menu.

Name: La Table de Florent
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In a converted barn that oozes charm, Florent Linard has created an ambiance that is entirely in keeping with his personal style. The open kitchen set beneath rafters sets the tone as he circulates between the kitchen and the tables to welcome guests and take orders. His sincere, honest cuisine revolves around ingredients and flavours: crispy beef tongue seasoned with bottarga, pan-fried foie gras; Dordogne trout cooked on one side, rillettes and escargot beurre blanc.

Name: La Table de Gabin - Maison de la Source
Description: A small country inn hidden away in a remote location is sometimes all it takes to pique our interest. Our curiosity was quickly rewarded in the form of the delicious food served by chef Gabin Bouguet (formerly of Le Donjon in Étretat), who is on a mission to keep things simple without compromising on indulgence. Hailing from the region himself, he is committed to showcasing its produce with skill in dishes that are full of character – expect a culinary treat from start to finish! After your meal, take a stroll to the cliffs a few hundred metres away – there you'll enjoy a beautiful view of Fécamp, as painted by Claude Monet.

Name: La Table de Haute-Serre
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: In the wine storehouse of a château in the heart of the vineyards, this restaurant exudes the very particular charm of truly authentic places. Charcuterie rack, butcher's block, ham slicer and cases of wine herald a wonderful moment of gourmet delights, rounded off by wines from the estate. Just delicious.

Name: La Table de Jean
Description: Originally from Béziers, this chef-owner has set up shop in a pedestrian street near the town hall. His small bistro comprises two dining spaces with exposed stone walls and sage green hues, square table tops and bistro chairs. The small terrace is exceedingly pleasant in fine weather. The seasons are reflected in his dishes, such as the delicately seasoned vanilla sea bass and delicious new take on poire belle Hélène.

Name: La Table de Jean
Description: Slightly off the main road to Albi, this establishment is fronted by a small terrace. In a vintage brasserie setting, the chef crafts a variety of local specialties: steak tartare, Aubrac beef burger or Aveyron aligot (cheese, garlic and mashed potatoes) with sausages.

Name: La Table de Jean-Mi
Address: Domaine de Champé, 14 rue des Champs-Navés, Bussang, 88540, France
Description: Jean-Mi is the endearing character who pours passion into looking after the natural estate that he and his family built from the ground up in the Ballons des Vosges region. Over the years, the open-air guinguette has been transformed into a cosy and welcoming restaurant, where regulars and newcomers alike linger over delicious seasonal dishes, many prepared with vegetables from the garden. A fresh perspective on the Hautes Vosges!

Name: La Table de Jean-Paul Tossens - Monastère de Saint-Mont
Description: To say this place is steeped in history is an understatement: the monastery, rebuilt several times since the Middle Ages, is said to stand on the site of a Roman oppidum. The chef signs a seasonal score designed to showcase noble ingredients and escorted by an irresistible lineup of desserts courtesy of his pastry-chef daughter, Carolyn. Guestrooms, pool and spa on site. Simpler fare at ‘Les Bérets Noirs’ bistro.

Name: La Table de Jeanne
Address: 14 avenue de la Grande-Motte, au Val-Claret, Tignes, 73320, France
Description: This mountainside restaurant, the brainchild of the Bouvier family (of Les Suites, Ursus, Panoramic), is depicted by generous dishes in which country produce takes pride of place. Warm, welcoming and a fine selection of reasonably - priced wines.

Name: La Table de Julien
Address: La Réserve de Beaulieu, 5 boulevard du Maréchal-Leclerc, Beaulieu-sur-Mer, 06310, France
Description: Supervised by chef Julien Roucheteau, La Table and its bargain-priced weekday menu are a welcome addition to the catering options offered by this high-class property. The Mediterranean score is firmly rooted in the region: confit tuna in a raw and cooked veggie salad, Provençal-style shoulder of lamb with creamy polenta or beef stew with gnocchi and Swiss chard. Pastry chef Benoit Jabouille stages a wickedly enticing sweet-toothed show at the end of the meal. Chic bistro vibe and a lovely terrace shaded by a pergola.

Name: La Table de Jérôme
Address: 26 rue de la République, Luzy, 58170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
Description: At his Table in the Hôtel du Morvan, chef Jérôme Raymond offers modern cooking based on regional produce. The set menu is inspired by the best of the season’s ingredients, with Charolais beef often a firm favourite. The 400-bin wine list concentrates, rightly so, on Burgundy. Comfortable rooms should you wish to stay longer.

Name: La Table de Kamiya
Address: 52 promenade de la Plage, Cagnes-sur-Mer, 06800, France
Description: Japanese chef Takayuki Kamiya and pastry chef Claire, his French-Japanese wife, have set up shop on the seafront of Cagnes-sur-Mer. The food is inspired by their adopted homeland (Provence) and their family backgrounds. Their set menus feature dishes inspired by France and Provence (sea bass in an almond crust, courgettes and pistou) and elevated by discreet Japanese touches (wakame, oloshi sauce, yuzu). Both the delicious peach dessert with verbena jelly and the rum baba, a house classic, are out of this world.

Name: La Table de L'Oléa
Address: 62 bis avenue des Ostréiculteurs, La Teste-de-Buch, 33260, France
Description: Located at the end of the harbour, this restaurant's terrace with rattan chairs boasts a peaceful view of the boats and oyster port, and feels like an invitation to indulge in a laid-back culinary interlude. The interior decor is also reminiscent of a boat, with its arched bar and light wood open kitchen. The chef Brice Tomico has perfected fresh seafood cuisine, featuring oysters from the hut next door and line-caught fish from Arcachon fish market.

Name: La Table de La Roya
Address: 468 route de la Roya, Saint-Florent, 20217, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Bang on Roya Beach with a matchless view of the bay of Saint Florent, this hotel-restaurant rolls out a huge terrace lined in gardens that stretches down to the seafront. At the helm are César and Fanny Combe whose globetrotting careers took them to luxury hotels in Polynesia and Vietnam. This cosmopolitan background adds a subtle edge to a modern Mediterranean score rich in vibrant, colourful flavours and dotted with exotic notes, illustrated by Tahitian-style tuna or the ginger, coconut or bok choy ingredients that jazz up some of the dishes. An idyllic setting against a backdrop of waves gently breaking on the shore.

Name: La Table de Laurent
Description: Laurent Prat uses quality produce (langoustine, monkfish etc) to create a range of classic and more modern dishes that are always seamlessly put together and have international influences: pan-fried gnocchi with spinach; seared prawns in a Mexican marinade; grilled grouper, aubergine roll with beetroot hummus. Afternoon tea with house-made pastries, served in an inviting wood-panelled interior.

Name: La Table de Luc
Address: 32 rue des Ponts-Neufs, Le Mans, 72000, France
Description: Luc Revert, a young chef from Le Mans, has returned to his roots after several years in the South of France and then in Paris, notably at Frédéric Simonin. The chef's generous and straightforward cooking is a joy. The small menu of carefully prepared dishes revolves around quality ingredients. The beef fillet is a good example of his style: tender grilled meat, soft gnocchi, a balanced garlic cream, black garlic condiment, rich jus and fragrant lovage oil. The clementine tartlet impresses with its crispy pastry, creamy yuzu-tarragon filling and vibrant clementine sorbet. Friendly and professional service.

Name: La Table de Léa
Address: 823 route de Saint-Maurice-d'Ibie (Le Petit Tournon), Villeneuve-de-Berg, 07170, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
Description: In this former barn, the chef concocts a traditional Gallic repertory to which she adds a melting pot of spices: foie gras with ginger, monkfish with zaatar or veal scattered in arabica notes and Batak berry-laced celery. In fine weather make a beeline for the lovely terrace shaded by chestnut trees.

Name: La Table de Marc Tupin - Hostellerie Saint-Germain
Description: Opposite the church, this engaging 17C coaching inn has been entirely refurbished in a low-key, contemporary vein. The chef sources fine local produce, often organic, to craft appetising dishes, occasionally peppered with creative touches, such as pink trout and nori seaweed. All of which is washed down with fine Jura wines. The cosy rooms are pleasant, and quieter overlooking the terrace.

Name: La Table de Marie-Ange
FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace
Description: The terrace overlooking the Aravis range is so mesmerising, it is difficult to tear oneself away. Marie-Ange aims to serve fine regional dishes oozing with authentic flavour: pan-seared cèpes, fillets of wild perch from Lake Geneva, fillet of beef simmered in mushrooms and grandma’s potato gratin, without forgetting the wickedly lavish dessert trolley. The interior sports old wood and farming tools – charming welcome.

Name: La Table de Maïna
Description: Bang in the heart of a peaceful street of Montrouge, get ready to embark on a culinary voyage from Asia to South America. Nikkei cuisine, a genuine fusion of Japanese and Peruvian culinary traditions, emerged in the late 19C when Japanese migrants discovered the criolla flavours of Peru. In this welcoming eatery, globetrotting chef, Maïna-Sophie Conil, explores this gourmet marriage in flavoursome, fusion-inspired recipes: fragrant ceviche laced in ginger and lime; crunchy tempura fish or carpaccio of Simmenthal beef enhanced by a truffle jus. The garden terrace is a hit in fine weather.

Name: La Table de Mentone
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Terrace,Wheelchair access
Description: Chef Sébastien Sanjou pops in from his nearby restaurant (Le Relais des Moines in Les Arcs-sur-Argens) to supervise the cooking at this fabulous restaurant set in the cellar of a wine estate, one of the finest in the Haut Var. As you take in the superlative surroundings (a panoramic landscape of vineyards and olive trees outside and a spacious designer-inspired interior), you can savour fine seasonal Provençal cuisine that makes the most of the estate's wide range of produce (courtesy of the hen house, orchard, vegetable garden, olive groves). For example, vegetable pot-au-feu with fresh herbs; stuffed saddle of rabbit with black olives and creamy polenta; baked pear with almonds and vanilla cream – washed down with a fine organic wine from the estate. A number of guestrooms are available to extend your stay in style.

Name: La Table de Mercuès
Address: Château de Mercuès, route du Château, Mercuès, 46090, France
FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Garden or park,Interesting wine list,Terrace
Description: Perched on a clifftop overlooking the Lot valley, this medieval castle is a majestic setting for contemporary fine dining and luxurious guestrooms. Tuck into delicious cuisine based on premium ingredients such as lobster, foie gras and Quercy pigeon, combined with more traditional local produce such as chanterelles and Rocamadour cheese. A single multi-course tasting menu is served in a refined interior set up within centuries-old stone walls. Chef Clément Costes devises a precise menu of perfectly cooked dishes, such as roast pigeon, which can be accompanied by one of the estate's fine wines. In fine weather, guests can dine on the terrace in the main courtyard.

Name: La Table de Michèle
Description: Michèle Brouet is a figure on the local gastronomy scene. Her restaurant is the reflection of her generosity and cheer, as is the atmosphere, which is welcoming with its various random objects and bouquets of flowers. Good food and good times are on the menu!

Name: La Table de Mina
Description: From your comfortable vantage point on a covered poolside terrace, savour the sweeping view over the sweet-scented scrubland and the sea.
